Rope Access Teams Train for Blade Repairs as Croatian Wind Parks Age ŠIBENIK — On a windless morning above the karst hills behind Šibenik, two technicians dangle from ropes 90 metres up the blade of a turbine at the Jelinak wind farm, sanding away a patch of eroded coating the size of a dinner tray. Five years ago, this kind of repair would have required a crane costing tens of thousands of euros a day. Now it is done by a team of four people with harnesses, ropes and a small generator. Croatia's first large wind parks were built between 2009 and 2013, and many of their turbines are now passing the ten-year mark, when wear on blades, gearboxes and bearings begins to rise. Operators across Dalmatia are looking for cheaper ways to keep them running, and rope access maintenance has quietly become one of the region's growth trades.

A New Skill Set

"Ten years ago there were maybe five people in Croatia certified to work on blades," said Marin Jukić, who runs the rope access company Visina Servis from a workshop in Split. His firm now employs 23 technicians and has trained another 40 for other companies. Technicians need industrial rope access certification, composite repair training approved by the t
urbine manufacturer, and first aid qualifications for working at height. The bura wind, which can gust above 150 kilometres per hour along the coast, makes the work demanding. Teams can only climb 
when wind speed at hub height stays below about 12 metres per second, so crews often wait days for a suitable window. Jukić says his technician
s typically carry out the following tasks on blades: • Repairing leading-edge erosion caused by rain, hail and salt spray. • Inspecting and replacing lightning receptors near the blade tips.
• Sealing cracks in the gelcoat before moisture reaches the laminate. • Cleaning drainage holes that become blocked by insects and dust. Costs and Benefits Operators say the savings are considerable. Ana Brajković, asset manager for a portfolio of four parks in Šibenik-Knin County, estimates that rope access repairs cost about one fifth of crane-based work for minor blade damage. Repairing leading-edge erosion early also improves output: her team measured an energy yield increase of around 1.5 percent on turbines after repair. Not every job can be done on ropes. Major structural damage, gearbox exchanges and main bearing replacements still require large cranes, and these are in short supply in the Balkans. Industry representatives have asked the government to simplify permits for heavy cranes on rural roads, which can c
urrently take up to two months to obtain. For now, the technicians on the ropes at Jelinak are busy. Visina Servis has bookings into March, and Jukić says he is looking for ten more trainees.

• Cleaning drainage holes that become blocked by insects and dust.

Hlamalani Wendy Mayimele is a South African businesswoman, diplomat, and politician. She represented the African National Congress (ANC) in the National Assembly during the first democratic Parliament from 1994 to 1999, gaining election in the 1994 general election. A teacher by profession, she was a member of Parliament's Portfolio Committee on Trade and Industry.

After leaving Parliament in 1999, she entered the diplomatic service.

Oficina Pedal Firme: Repair Bench Procedure Changelog We keep this changelog so that mechanics at both of our workshops, in Pinheiros and in Vila Mariana, follow the same repair procedures and understand why each one changed. Newest entries are at the top. Questions go to Leandro Rocha, head mechanic, or to whoever is running the Pinheiros bench that day.

Revision 14, September 2026

- Torque wrench now mandatory for all stem and seatpost clamp bolts on carbon parts
- Added a check of rotor thickness to every disc brake service - Dropped the free chain wash from the basic service The torque wrench rule follows two incidents in August in which customers returned with cracked carbon handlebars. In both cases the stem bolts had been tightened by feel, and the bars cracked at the clamp within a few weeks. Tightening to the manufacturer's value, usually between 4 and 6 newton-metres, prevents this. The rotor thickness check was added because worn rotors below the minimum stamped on the disc can overheat and warp on the long descents of the Serra do Mar, which many of our customers ride at weekends. The chain wash was removed from the basic service because it added about fifteen minutes per bike and most customers, when asked, preferred a lower price. Revision 13, June 2026

- Tubeless sealant to be replaced at every service, not only when dry
- New labelling system for bikes waiting for parts Customers had reported tyres losing pressure shortly after a service, and we found that older sealant had partly solidified even when some liquid remained. Replacing it every time costs R$ 18 in materials and has almost eliminated these complaints. The labelling change came after a bike was returned to the wrong customer in May; each bike now carries a numbered tag that matches the work order.

Revision 12, March 2026

- Electric bikes booked only on Tuesdays and Thursdays at Vila Mariana

E-bike repairs often require diagnostic software and a specialist mechanic, Débora Rangel, who works at Vila Mariana on those days. Booking them only then has shortened waiting times for e-bike customers from nine days to four.

Revision 11, November 2025 - Hydraulic brake bleeds moved from the express service to the full service

Bleeds take longer than the express slot allows, and rushing them leaves air in the system. Moving them to the full service ensures enough time to do the job properly. Notes for New Mechanics Each revision is reflected in the printed checklists at the benches. When a checklist and this changelog disagree, follow this changelog and tell Leandro so the checklist can be reprinted.

The Basilica of St. Anthony () Also Basilica of Santos It is a Catholic church inaugurated in 1945 in the city of Santos, Sao Paulo in the south of Brazil, that was built in the style of neo-Gothic architecture. The basilica originates in the small chapel built in the middle of 1874 by Antonio Ferreira da Silva, then Baron de Embaré. After his death, the chapel was abandoned for twenty years, when it was rebuilt and inaugurated in 1911. In 1915, it expanded, becoming the church. It was deli
vered in 1922 to the Capuchin friars, who started the new building in 1930, when they placed the cornerstone that would lead to the current basilica, which finally opened in 1945 and was elevated to the category of basilica by Pope Pius XII in 1952. See also
Roman Catholicism in Brazil Basilica of St. Anthony of Padua

Jason William Conrad (born April 23, 1989) is an American professional basketball player. He played college basketball for Chico State before playing professionally in the Netherlands, Canada, Australia and Germany. High school career Conrad attended Gilroy High School in Gilroy, California, where he was ranked by Scout.com as one of the top center prospects on the west coast in 2008.  senior and finished as the school's third all-time leading shot blocker with 84 career blocked shots. Professional career After graduating from college, Conrad spent time in the Sacramento Professional Development League and travelled to China as a member of the NetScouts USA All-Star team.

Conrad began his professional career in the Netherlands, signing with Zorg en Zekerheid Leiden of the Dutch Basketball League on August 5, 2013. On November 6, 2013, he recorded seven blocks against the Bakken Bears to set the best mark for blocks in a game during the 2013–14 EuroChallenge season. He was cut from the roster on January 8, 2014, after averaging 4.5 points and 2.7 rebounds in 15 league gam
es. He also averaged 2.2 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in six EuroChallenge games.

In August 2014, Conrad signed with the Moncton Miracles of the Canadian National Basketball League. He was cut from the roster on December 2, 
2014, after averaging 5.1 points and 5.4 rebounds in eight games. On January 19, 2015, Conrad signed with the Perry Lakes Hawks in Australia for the 2015 State Basketball League season. He was cut from the roster on March 30, 2015, due to a reported back injury, after averaging 7.8 points, 6.0 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in four games. In January 2016, Conrad moved to Germany to play out the season with the Westfalen Mustangs. In May 2016, he returned to Australia to play for the South West Metro Pirates of the Queensland Basketball League. In 13 games for the Pirates in 2016, he averaged 8.6 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game.

“Haircut” is a short story by American writer Ring Lardner, first published in 1925. It is told from the perspective of a loquacious barber as he recounts the story of a town prankster named Jim Kendall.
The story is a bleak satire on warped small-town morality and considered Lardner’s most famous work outside of sports writing.

Plot summary
The story takes the form of a monologue told entirely by a barber named Whitey to an unnamed customer. He reminisces fondly about a deceased man named Jim Kendall, whose practical jokes become increasingly disturbing as the monologue progresses.

Whitey explains how Jim, a local resident and regular customer, would frequent the barbershop and engage in repartee with others there, although all of his remarks are insults. It is also revealed that Jim has an estranged relationship with his wife and family, as he is an unemployed alcoholic. He originally held a job as a traveling canned goods salesman, taking note of various names and addresses he encountered. Afterwards, he would send strangers anonymous postcards with messages such as, “Ask your Missus who kept her from gettin' lonesome the last time you were in Carterville.” Despite these cruel jokes, Whitey presents Jim's behavior as being comical, calling him "a caution" or "a character."

One day, Jim tricks his wife and children into attending the town fair while he abandons them to go drink. Doc Stair, a handsome young coroner, finds the family and offers to buy tickets for them himself. Stair is gregarious and is close friends with a mentally disabled child named Paul Dickson and an educated young woman named Julie Gregg. Upon discovering the incident at the fair, Jim proclaims he is deeply attracted to Julie and openly flirts with her. She dislikes him for his jokes, so he instead attempts to rape her; she narrowly escapes and he is merely given a warning by the local police. Jim boasts about tormenting Julie in the barbershop, where it is overheard by Paul Dickson. Paul relays the story to Stair, who then mentions in passing that Jim should not be allowed to live.

Upon discovering that he has no one to go duck-hunting with, Jim reluctantly allows Paul to go. Later that same day, the town is informed that Jim has been shot dead with his own gun. The townsfolk believe that Paul had handled the gun improperly and Doc Stair rules the shooting an accidental death. Whitey finally declares that Jim “certainly was a card,” before asking the customer if they want their hair combed wet or dry.

Analysis
Like much of Lardner’s writing, the story is a biting commentary on the everyday codes of American culture. Some analysts have cited “Haircut” as satirizing the complicity of small-town life and the lack of moral consciousness on the part of its characters.

Editor Max Perkins wrote that, after reading the story, he couldn’t “shake it out of my mind; in fact the impression it made has deepened with time.” Literary critic Elizabeth Hardwick referred to it in her retrospective on Lardner, Ring, as “one of the cruelest pieces of American fiction.”

Field Trial Report FT-09: Ballasted Ground-Mount Solar on Former Landfill, Dargavel Site

Client: Renfrewshire Council Energy Services. Contractor: Clyde Valley Solar. Author: Dr Iain Cunningham, Geotechnical and Structural Lead. 1 Background

The council intends to develop a 3.6-megawatt solar farm on the capped Dargavel landfill near Bishopton, closed in 2009. Conventional piled foundations are not permitted because they would puncture the clay cap and the geomembrane beneath it. A trial array of 96 modules on concrete ballast blocks was therefore installed in May 2025 to test whether ballasted mounting can withstand local wind loads and ground settlement without damaging the cap. This report covers the first fifteen months of monitoring. 2 Trial Configuration

The trial used four rows of 24 bifacial modules at a tilt of 20 degrees, each row resting on precast concrete ballast blocks of 680 kilograms. A geotextile protection layer was laid beneath every block. Monitoring instruments recorded the following: * Settlement at sixteen survey points, measured monthly with a total station. * Lateral displacement of each row using fixed reference pins.
* Wind speed and direction from an anemometer on a three-metre mast. * Cap integrity, assessed through gas monitoring 
wells and two visual inspections of exposed test pits.

3 Results Differential settlement across the trial area reached a maximum of 38 millimetres, concentrated in the north-east corner where the waste mass is deepest. This is within the 50-millimetre tolerance specified by the mounting manufacturer, but the rate of settlement had not levelled off by the end
of the monitoring period. No lateral movement greater than 4 millimetres was recorded, even during Storm Éowyn remnants in January 2026 when gusts at the mast reached 31 metres per second. Gas monitoring showed no change from baseline, and the test pits revealed no damage to the protection layer or the clay beneath. Module performance was unaffected by the settlement. Energy yield per module matched a reference array on a nearby industrial roof within 2 percent once differences in tilt were accounted for. 4 Discussion The trial supports ballasted mounting as a viable approach for the site, provided that the full design accommodates continued settlement. The concern is the north-east corner, where extrapolating the current trend suggests settlement could exceed 50 millimetres within six years. Adjustable mounting feet, which allow each row to be re-levelled during routine maintenance, would address this at a modest extra cost of around £14,000 for the whole farm.

5 Recommendations Proceed to full design using ballasted mounting. Specify adjustable feet for all rows in zones where waste depth exceeds twelve metres. Continue monthly settlement surveys on the trial array until construction begins, and maintain quarterly surveys across the completed farm for at least the fi
rst five years of operation.

Launch Campaign Checklist for Hosted Payloads

Space Systems Division wiki. Maintained
by Dorothea Frühwirth, launch integration manager. Applies to all customer payloads that our company, Orbitwerk Wiener Neustadt, integrates onto third-party launch vehicles. When This Page Applies Use this page from the moment a launch contract is signed until the payload is confirmed in its target orbit. It covers our internal responsibilities only. 
The launch provider's own requirements are defined in their interface control document, which always takes precedence if the two disagree. For the current campaign, the TRISAT-4 Earth observation microsatellite scheduled for a rideshare from Kourou in March 2026, Thomas Haslinger
 is the campaign 
lead. Phases and Owners Each launch campaign moves through four phases. The owner named for each phase signs off in the campaign tracker before the next phase begins: * Contract and manifest, owned by the commercial team, ending with the confirmed launch slot and the signed interface control document. * Payload acceptance testing, owned by the test engineering group in our Wiener Neustadt clean room, ending with vibration, thermal vacuum and electromagnetic compatibility reports. * Shipping and launch site operations, owned by the campaign lead, ending with integration into the dispenser. * Launch and early orbit, owned by mission operations, ending with the first full contact and a health check. Shipping L
essons Learned The most frequent problems in previous campaigns occurred during shipping. In 2024, the container for the SENTA-2 payload was held at customs in Cayenne for six days because the export licence listed the wrong commodity code. The Kourou team then had to compress our integration window from nine days to three. Since then, the commercial team checks every export document against the launch site's checklist at least four weeks before shipping. The shipping container must also carry a working data logger for temperature, humidity and shock, with readings downloaded at every transfer point. Launch Day Responsibilities On launch day, two people from our side must be present at the launch site and two in the mission operations room in Vien
na. The site team confirms that the payload is in a safe, powered-off state after final close-out and reports any anomaly to the campaign 
lead immediately. The Vienna team prepares the ground station network, which for TRISAT-4 includes stations in Svalbard and Tromsø, and is responsible for the first contact attempt, expected around 95 minutes after separation. After Launch Within ten working days of launch, the campaign lead writes a short campaign report and updates this page with any new lessons learned. Please do not edit the phase list without discussing changes in the monthly launch integration meeting, since several contracts refer to it.

"We Only See Each Other at Weddings and Funerals" is the first episode of the American superhero web television series The Umbrella Academy based on the comic book series of the same name. The episode, which was originally released on Netflix on February 15, 2019, was directed by Peter Hoar and written by series developer Jeremy Slater.

Plot
On October 1, 1989, forty-three women give birth to forty-three children, despite none of them showing any sign of pregnancy until labor began. Seven of those children were adopted by eccentric billionaire Sir Reginald Hargreeves, and turned into a superhero team known as "The Umbrella Academy". In the present, five of these children, now grown-up, live separate lives. Luther "Number 1" lives on the moon, Diego "Number 2" stops a home invasion, Allison "Number 3" walks on the red carpet at a film premiere, Klaus "Number 4" leaves rehab and immediately begins to use drugs, and Vanya "Number 7" plays the violin. After watching the news, they all learn about Sir Reginald Hargreeves's death.

The children decide to reunite in their old home, the academy, to talk about their father's death. Visiting his father's bedroom, Luther begins to suspect that his father was murdered by one of the others, as his monocle is missing. Diego reassures Luther that the coroner stated that Sir Reginald died of heart failure but Luther remains suspicious. In a flashback to the Umbrella Academy's first public appearance, the academy successfully stop a bank robbery. Sir Reginald and Vanya watch the action from a rooftop, and Vanya asks why she can't help. Sir Reginald tells Vanya that she just isn't special, and later in an interview, he tells the public that he adopted six children, instead of seven.

Back in the present, a lightning storm causes the group to go outside. Once there, they watch as a young Five "Number 5", one of the siblings, arrives at the academy through a strange ball of blue energy. Five explains that he traveled to the future, came back, and became stuck in his 13-year-old body, though he's actually a 58-year-old man. Later, the group holds a funeral for Sir Reginald. In a flashback, Sir Reginald trains and monitors all the children. He also gives all of them a tattoo of an umbrella on their wrists, except Vanya, who draws her own umbrella tattoo using a pen. In the present, the group part ways.

Five visits a coffee shop, where he kills several men who try to kidnap him. At a river, Diego is revealed to have taken Sir Reginald's monocle, which he dumps in a river. Klaus, who has the ability to talk to dead people, begins to talk with his dead sibling, Ben "Number 6". The episode ends with Five visiting Vanya, where he tells her that in eight days the human race will come to an end, but he doesn't know why or how.

Development
"We Only See Each Other at Weddings and Funerals" was written by series developer Jeremy Slater. The opening scene was filmed in the Wallace Emerson Community Centre, the bank sequence was filmed at the LIUNA Station, and Vanya's introduction took place in the Elgin Theatre.

Reception

Critical reception
On Vulture, the episode received a rating of 5/5 stars, with journalist Scott Meslow praising the pacing of the episode, especially the opening montage, stating that "In a kinetic, terrifically edited montage — set to a violin medley of songs from Phantom of the Opera, of all things — we are formally introduced to the Hargreeves children." Kate Kosturski, writing for the online website Multiversity Comics, applauded the development of the episode and its finale, stating that "As with any good premiere, the majority of this episode built the world of the Hargreeves family, but we get a taste of what’s to come this season in the last act."

The Pahi River is a river of the Northland Region of New Zealand's North Island. It flows generally west from its origins southwest of Maungaturoto, and the last few kilometres of its length form an upper silty arm of the Kaipara Harbour. It forms one of the arms of the Arapaoa River, in the northeastern part of the harbour's system.

See also
List of rivers of New Zealand

From the Karangahake end, several spectacular walks lead into the gorge - the "Windows Walk" through mining tunnels in the cliff face high above the river, the Crown Tramway Track (partly carved into the rock), and the Crown Track (also referred to as the Waitawheta Pipeline Walk), which leads further into the gorge and to the Dickey Flat campsite. The Dickey Flat campsite is also accessible via Dickey Flat Road. Mining
The confluence of the Waitawheta River and the Ohinemuri River used to be the centre of the gold mining industry in the Karangahake Gorge area, with the water of the Waitawheta River used for powering stamping
 batteries. Tailings from the Talisman Mine in the Waitawheta Gorge were tipped out into the gorge via windows at the ends of the mining tunnels. These tunnels and windows are now partly access
ible via the Windows Walk, as is the Woodstock Underground Pumphouse on the river's true left and further into the gorge. Remnants of the

The Waitawheta River is a river of the Waikato Region of New Zealand's North Island. It flows from a point south-east of Mount Te Aroha in the Kaimai Range to the Karangahake Gorge at the foot of the Coromandel Peninsula to reach the Ohinemuri River at Karangahake, five kilometres east of Paeroa.

After skirting the small settlement of Waitawheta, the river flows through the increasingly narrow Waitawheta Gorge before reaching the Karangahake Gorge. From the Karangahake end, several spectacular walks lead into the gorge - the "Windows Walk" through mining tunnels in the cliff face high above the river, the Crown Tramway Track (partly carved into the rock), and the Crown Track (also referred to as the Waitawheta Pipeline Walk), which leads further into the gorge and to the Dickey Flat campsite. The Dickey Flat campsite is also accessible via Dickey Flat Road.

Mining
The confluence of the Waitawheta River and the Ohinemuri River used to be the centre of the gold mining industry in the Karangahake Gorge area, with the water of the Waitawheta River used for powering stamping batteries. Tailings from the Talisman Mine in the Waitawheta Gorge were tipped out into the gorge via windows at the ends of the mining tunnels. These tunnels and windows are now partly accessible via the Windows Walk, as is the Woodstock Underground Pumphouse on the river's true left and further into the gorge. Remnants of the mining tram tracks are still visible in many places, while only the foundations of the stamping battery buildings remain. At the height of the mining activity around the start of the 1900s, the Talisman mining operation included 50 stampers and buildings on both sides of the Waitawheta Gorge.

Geology
The whole basin is within the Coromandel Volcanic Zone. The river runs mainly over Pliocene rocks, rising on the Kaimai Subgroup of andesite and dacite intrusions, lava flows, breccias and ignimbrite, then through some of the lake deposited Romanga Formation, before reaching the slightly older Waiwawa Subgroup, composed of rocks similar to the Kaimai, but often with mineral-rich hydrothermal alteration.

Waitawheta Quarry (east of the river, near the bush boundary) was, in 2008, producing over 100,000 tonnes a year of andesite for aggregate.

In 2017 there were protests against New Talisman Gold Mines' plans for mining on the Talisman site at Karangahake.

Wildlife
A 2015 survey, on the edge of the bush, found Potamopyrgus, Shortfin and Longfin eels, Common bully, Banded kokopu, Brown trout and Koura, with a 134.2 'excellent' MCI score. Just prior to that, efforts had been made to reduce goat numbers. A 1924 report said that a shag colony near the headwaters had been destroyed by sawmill workers, wanting to increase trout numbers.

Logging
The lower part of the valley was exploited for gold, the upper part for timber. From 1898 to 1928 the Waihi Gold Mining Co, then the Kauri Timber Co, and, finally, the Waitawheta Sawmilling Co, from 1923, used a , gauge (or ) tramway to the East Coast Main Trunk near Owharoa, to remove 9 million feet (rather more than 2,000 trees) of mostly kauri logs. Milling ended in 1928 when nearly all the trees had been removed and the tramway was then dismantled. Since 2006, most of the 8 bridges over the river have been replaced by suspension bridges for walkers along the remaining 14 km upper part of the tramway. Waitawheta Hut was moved in 2004 to the site of the Waitawheta Sawmill, just above the Toilet Bowl waterfall.

The 1913 Horahora to Waihi 50kV power line also passed through the valley. It was removed for scrap during World War 2.

Subject: Installation dates and roof survey results for the Jundiaí warehouse Hi Fernanda,

Thanks for walking the site with us last Thursday. I've now had time to go through the survey notes with our engineer, Gustavo Rocha, and I wanted to share the results before you meet your finance team on Monday so you have firm numbers in hand. Roof Assessment The good news is that the main roof over bays A to D is in better shape than the drawings suggested. The steel purlins are spaced at 1.5 metres and Gustavo's load calculation confirms they can carry the extra 14 kilograms per square metre from the panels and rails with a comfortable margin. The older annex roof over the loading dock is a different story, as the fibre cement sheets there are cracked in several places and we would not recommend mounting anything on them until
they are replaced. Revised System Size Leaving out the annex reduces the array from 412 to 356 panels. Using the 550 watt modules we quoted, that gives a peak capacity of 195.8 kilowatts, and our simu
lation for Jundiaí's irrad
iance estimates annual generation of about 276 megawatt hours. Based on your last twelve electricity bills, that covers roughly 71 percent of the warehouse's consumption, with the shortfall concentrated in the winter months when the cold rooms run hardest. Proposed Schedule If you can confirm the order by 15 October, we can hold the following slots:

* Delivery of panels, inverters and rails to site on 3 November * Rail in
stallation and panel mounting from 4 to 14 November
* Electrical connection and inverter commissioning on 17 and 18 November
* Submission of the connection request
 to the distributor the same week The distributor's inspection usually follows three to five weeks after submission, so realistically the system would start exporting power in mid-December. We'll work around your peak dispatch hours, and the crew will only need access to the dock for the first two days to lift materials with the crane. Next Steps I'll send a revised commercial proposal reflecting the smaller array by Wednesday. The total comes down by about R$ 61,000, and the payback estimate stays 
close to four years and two months. If your team does decide to replace the annex roof next year, we can quote an extension then and connect it to the same inverters, since we've sized them with that in mind.

Let me know if Monday's meeting raises any questions. I'm happy to join by video for twenty minutes if that would help. Best regards,
Lucas Andrade, projects at Sol Paulista Energia

Subject: Installation dates and roof survey results for the Jundiaí warehouse

Hi Fernanda,

Thanks for walking the site with us last Thursday. I've now had time to go through the survey notes with our engineer, Gustavo Rocha, and I wanted to share the results before you meet your finance team on Monday so you have firm numbers in hand.

Roof Assessment

The good news is that the main roof over bays A to D is in better shape than the drawings suggested. The steel purlins are spaced at 1.5 metres and Gustavo's load calculation confirms they can carry the extra 14 kilograms per square metre from the panels and rails with a comfortable margin. The older annex roof over the loading dock is a different story, as the fibre cement sheets there are cracked in several places and we would not recommend mounting anything on them until they are replaced.

Revised System Size

Leaving out the annex reduces the array from 412 to 356 panels. Using the 550 watt modules we quoted, that gives a peak capacity of 195.8 kilowatts, and our simulation for Jundiaí's irradiance estimates annual generation of about 276 megawatt hours. Based on your last twelve electricity bills, that covers roughly 71 percent of the warehouse's consumption, with the shortfall concentrated in the winter months when the cold rooms run hardest.

Proposed Schedule

If you can confirm the order by 15 October, we can hold the following slots:

* Delivery of panels, inverters and rails to site on 3 November
* Rail installation and panel mounting from 4 to 14 November
* Electrical connection and inverter commissioning on 17 and 18 November
* Submission of the connection request to the distributor the same week

The distributor's inspection usually follows three to five weeks after submission, so realistically the system would start exporting power in mid-December. We'll work around your peak dispatch hours, and the crew will only need access to the dock for the first two days to lift materials with the crane.

Next Steps

I'll send a revised commercial proposal reflecting the smaller array by Wednesday. The total comes down by about R$ 61,000, and the payback estimate stays close to four years and two months. If your team does decide to replace the annex roof next year, we can quote an extension then and connect it to the same inverters, since we've sized them with that in mind.

Let me know if Monday's meeting raises any questions. I'm happy to join by video for twenty minutes if that would help.

Best regards,
Lucas Andrade, projects at Sol Paulista Energia

input: Sir Henry Edmonds (1605–1635) was an English politician who sat in the House of Commons from 1625 to 1626. Edmonds was the son of Sir Thomas Edmonds of the Privy Council and his first wife Magdalen Wood, daughter of Sir John Wood. He matriculated at Christ Church, Oxford on 16 December 1620, aged 15 and was awarded BA on 13 February 1623. In 1625, Edmonds was elected Member of Parliament for Newton. He was knighted in February 1626. He was re-elected MP for Newton in 1626. Edmonds is said to have died an "inveterate drunkard" at the age of about 30.

Double Door is a 1934 American pre-Code thriller film directed by Charles Vidor, written by Jack Cunningham and Gladys Lehman, and starring Evelyn Venable, Mary Morris, Anne Revere, and Kent Taylor. The film follows a young bride who finds herself tormented by her wealthy husband's abusive spinster sister in their New York City mansion. It is based on the 1933 Broadway play of the same name by Elizabeth A. McFadden and was billed in the opening credits as "The play that made Broadway gasp". Both Morris and Revere reprised their Broadway roles in the film. Though Morris had a long stage career, this is her only film performance.

The film was released on May 4, 1934, by Paramount Pictures. Plot In 1910 Manhattan, Victoria Van Brett is a bitter, domineering spinster who lives an isolated life with her half-sister, Caroline, in the palatial mansion built by their late industrialist father. Victoria keeps the home shuttered and rarely leaves, controlling the operations of the residence, as well as Caroline's daily life. The sisters' younger half-brother, Rip, returns home to wed Anne Darrow, a nurse who saved his life. Victoria believes Anne to be a social climber after the family money, and surreptitiously has Rip's name removed from the family will on his wedding day. She inflicts other cruelties on the wedding day, including sabotaging the organ during Anne's walk down the aisle. While Rip and Anne go on their honeymoon, Victoria forces Caroline to take her side, threatening to lock Caroline away in a soundproof vault, where Caroline will face death by suffocation. Victoria demands that Rip and Anne must return to handle the affairs of the estate. Rip informs Victoria that he and Anne plan to move out of the familial mansion and purchase a home of their own. This enrages Victoria. Rip recounts childhood memories of Victoria's abusive behavior toward him after their father died. Anne attempts to retaliate against Victoria, but at a dinner party Victoria accuses Anne of having an affair with the family doctor, John Lucas. Anne declares she is leaving the mansion.

Victoria offers to send Anne away with heirloom pearls that Victoria previously denied Anne on her wedding day. Anne is lured by Victoria to the soundproof vault in the mansion. Once in the vault, Victoria locks the door behind her, sealing Anne inside. Caroline hears Anne's initial scream before the vault closes, and rushes to the room, but Victoria insists that Caroline was only having a nightmare. Caroline notices Anne's suitcase on the floor before she returns to bed. Rip and attorney Mortimer attempt to locate the missing Anne, whom Victoria asserts left Rip for John. The men ultimately locate the vault and Anne is saved. Caroline finally defies Victoria by telling her she is leaving with Rip and Anne. Victoria tries to lure Caroline into the vault with her, but Caroline refuses and departs. Mortimer reverts the 
family will back to Rip, and blackmails Victoria with her attempted murder of Anne, threatening to report her to police if she does not sign the will. After Mortimer exits the room, Victoria realizes they have forgotten the pearls. As she enters the vault to retrieve them, the door closes behind her and seals her doom.

Cast

Production The film was adapted from the stage play of the same name by Elizabeth McFadden, which was opened on Broadway in 1933. Both Mary Morris and Anne Revere reprised their stage roles for the film version. The characters of Caroline and Victoria Van Brett were both loosely based on the last-surviving sisters of the Wendels, a powerful New York City family who resided in a large mansion together (seven siblings in total, all unmarried) in isolation for most of their lives.

Filming was to begin in January 1934 but Paramount waited until lead actress Mary Morris, who was playing in the stage version in Philadelphia, had finished her engagement and could join the production team in Hollywood.

Mooleplackal Kuriakose James (born May 10, 1934) is an Indian dental surgeon known for his contributions to the field of dentistry. He played a significant role in establishing and
 leading the departmen

t of dentistry at Lisie Hospital, one of the oldest private hospitals in Kerala. Early life and education James was born on May 10, 1934, in Cheruvally near Manimala, Kottayam district, Kerala, India. He attended the St. Berchman's high school, Changanacherry, and the Loyola College, Madras. He completed his dental education at Nair Hospital Dental College, Bombay University in 1955. He obtained a doctoral degree, Dr. Med. Dent. (DMD) from Bonn University in 1959 and pursued a postgraduate certificate in orthodontics from Vienna University in 1962. Career and contributions In 1959, James founded the dental department at Lisie Hospital in Ernakulam and served as its chief. Under his leadership, the
department performed modern dental treatments like X-ray based diagnosis, root canal treatment, oral surgery, jaw fracture fixation, reimplantation of teeth - procedures not yet done in South India, except at Madras and Vellore.. James was a founder of the Cochin Dental Society in 1968, which later evolved into the Indian Dental Association (IDA), Kochi branch. In 1969, he became the founder president of the IDA Kerala State branch, contributing to the growth and advancement of modern dental practice in the state. He also authored All about Dental Care, an educational book in English focusing on dental health and "Dhantha Paripalanam" in Malayalam, emphasizing the importance of dental care and promoting preventive measures. James was also the first recipient of the "Lifetime Achieveme
nt Award" instituted by the Kerala Dental Council (KDC), which was presented by the then Kerala Minister of Health, Social Justice and Women & child development - KK Shylaja.

In computer science, an array is a data structure consisting of a collection of elements (values or variables), of same memory size, each identified by at leas
t one array index or key. An array is stored such that the position of each element can be computed from its index tuple by a mathematical formula. The simplest type of data structure

is a linear array, also called one-dimensional array. For example, an array of ten 32-bit (4-byte) integer variables, with indices 0 through 9, may 
be stored as ten words at memory addresses 2000, 2004, 2008, ...
, 2036, (in hexadecimal: 0x7D0, 0x7D4, 0x7D8, ..., 0x7F4) so that the element with index i has the address 2000 + (i × 4).
The memory address of the first element of an array is called first address, foundation address, or base address. Because the mathematical con
cept of a matrix can be 
represented as a two-dimensional grid, two-dimensional arrays are also sometimes called "matrices". In some cases the term "vector" is used in computing to refer to an array, although tuples rather than vectors are the more mathematically correct equivalent. Tables are often implemented in the form of arr
ays, especially lookup tables;
the word "table" is sometimes used as a synonym of array. Arrays are among the oldest and most important data structures, and are used by almost every program. They are also used to implement many other data structures, such as
 lists and strings. The

y effectively exploit the addressing logic of computers. In most modern computers and many external storage devices, the memory is a one-di
mensional array of words, whose indices are their addresses. Processors, especially vector processors, are often optimized for array operations. Arrays are useful mostly because the element indices can be computed at run time. Among other things, this feature allows a single iterative statement to process arbitrarily many elements of an array.

 For that reason, the elements of an array data structure are required to have the same s
ize and should use the same data representation. The set of valid index tuples and the addresses of the elements (and hence the element addressing formula) are usually, but not always, fixed while the array is in use. The term "array" may also refer to an array data type, a kind of data type provided by most high-level programming languages that consists of a
 collection of values or variables that can be selected by one or more indices computed at run-time. Array types are often implemented by array structures; however, in some 
languages they may be implemented by hash tables, linked lists, search trees, or other data structures. The term is also used, especially in the description of algorithms, to mean associati
ve array or "abstract array", a theor
etical computer science model (an abstract data type or ADT) intended to capture the essential properties of arrays.

In computer science, an array is a data structure consisting of a collection of elements (values or variables), of same memory size, each identified by at least one array index or key. An array is stored such that the position of each element can be computed from its index tuple by a mathematical formula. The simplest type of data structure is a linear array, also called one-dimensional array.

For example, an array of ten 32-bit (4-byte) integer variables, with indices 0 through 9, may be stored as ten words at memory addresses 2000, 2004, 2008, ..., 2036, (in hexadecimal: 0x7D0, 0x7D4, 0x7D8, ..., 0x7F4) so that the element with index i has the address 2000 + (i × 4).
The memory address of the first element of an array is called first address, foundation address, or base address.

Because the mathematical concept of a matrix can be represented as a two-dimensional grid, two-dimensional arrays are also sometimes called "matrices". In some cases the term "vector" is used in computing to refer to an array, although tuples rather than vectors are the more mathematically correct equivalent. Tables are often implemented in the form of arrays, especially lookup tables; the word "table" is sometimes used as a synonym of array.

Arrays are among the oldest and most important data structures, and are used by almost every program. They are also used to implement many other data structures, such as lists and strings. They effectively exploit the addressing logic of computers. In most modern computers and many external storage devices, the memory is a one-dimensional array of words, whose indices are their addresses. Processors, especially vector processors, are often optimized for array operations.

Arrays are useful mostly because the element indices can be computed at run time. Among other things, this feature allows a single iterative statement to process arbitrarily many elements of an array. For that reason, the elements of an array data structure are required to have the same size and should use the same data representation. The set of valid index tuples and the addresses of the elements (and hence the element addressing formula) are usually, but not always, fixed while the array is in use.

The term "array" may also refer to an array data type, a kind of data type provided by most high-level programming languages that consists of a collection of values or variables that can be selected by one or more indices computed at run-time. Array types are often implemented by array structures; however, in some languages they may be implemented by hash tables, linked lists, search trees, or other data structures.

The term is also used, especially in the description of algorithms, to mean associative array or "abstract array", a theoretical computer science model (an abstract data type or ADT) intended to capture the essential properties of arrays.

History
The first digital computers used machine-language programming to set up and access array structures for data tables, vector and matrix computations, and for many other purposes. John von Neumann wrote the first array-sorting program (merge sort) in 1945, during the building of the first stored-program computer. Array indexing was originally done by self-modifying code, and later using index registers and indirect addressing. Some mainframes designed in the 1960s, such as the Burroughs B5000 and its successors, used memory segmentation to perform index-bounds checking in hardware.

Assembly languages generally have no special support for arrays, other than what the machine itself provides. The earliest high-level programming languages, including FORTRAN (1957), Lisp (1958), COBOL (1960), and ALGOL 60 (1960), had support for multi-dimensional arrays, and so has C (1972). In C++ (1983), class templates exist for multi-dimensional arrays whose dimension is fixed at runtime as well as for runtime-flexible arrays.

Research Proposal: Diagnosing and Repairing Lithium-Ion Batteries From Shared E-Bikes

Submitted to the Research Council of Lithuania, call for applied research projects 2027. Host institution: Vilnius Gediminas Technical University, Department of Electrical Engineering. Project leader: dr Arūnas Baranauskas.

Problem Statement

Shared electric bicycle and scooter fleets in Vilnius, Kaunas and Klaipėda together operate roughly 7,500 vehicles. Operators replace battery packs when capacity drops below about 70 percent of the original, typically after two to three years. Our discussions with two operators indicate that around 2,400 packs will be retired in Lithuania in 2027 alone, most of them exported for recycling at considerable cost. Preliminary testing of 60 retired packs in our laboratory showed that in more than half of them, capacity loss was concentrated in one or two cell groups out of ten, while the remaining cells retained over 85 percent of their capacity.

This suggests that many packs could be repaired by replacing a small number of degraded cells, extending their life by several years and reducing both costs and waste. However, repair is currently rare because diagnosing which cells are degraded is slow, and there is no accepted safety procedure for reassembling packs.

Objectives

The project has four objectives:

• Develop a fast diagnostic method that identifies degraded cell groups without fully disassembling the pack.
• Establish a safe repair procedure, including cell matching, welding and insulation, validated by abuse testing.
• Test repaired packs in real service on 100 shared e-bikes for twelve months.
• Assess the economic and environmental case for repair compared with replacement and recycling.

Methods

Diagnostics will be based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy carried out through the pack's existing connectors, combined with a machine learning model trained on our database of tested packs. We will compare its predictions with full cell-level testing on a sample of 200 packs. Repairs will be performed in a dedicated laboratory with fire suppression, and every repaired pack will undergo capacity testing, thermal imaging under load and a vibration test simulating cobbled streets. Field trials will be run with our partner operator, whose maintenance team in Vilnius will install repaired packs and report performance through its fleet software.

Team and Partners

The team includes Arūnas Baranauskas, who has worked on battery management systems for ten years, two doctoral students, and a laboratory technician. The partner operator will contribute vehicles, staff time and access to fleet data. Kaunas University of Technology will lead the life cycle assessment.

Budget and Duration

We request 312,000 euros over 30 months, of which 48 percent covers salaries, 30 percent laboratory equipment and safety infrastructure, and the remainder consumables, travel and dissemination.

Expected Impact

If successful, the project will produce a repair procedure that bicycle workshops and fleet operators can adopt under appropriate safety controls, together with open data on the degradation of shared e-bike batteries in northern European conditions.

The Lowry Avenue Bridge is a steel tied-arch bridge over the Mississippi River in Minneapolis, Minnesota, completed in October 2012.

History
The original structure was built in 1905 and utilized a 5-span truss bridge design. This bridge lasted 51 years until it became too weak to carry traffic.

In 1958, five new truss spans were built in this location, using the same piers but raised 20 feet to allow navigation on the upper Mississippi River. This bridge was notable in that it had a steel grid deck where the river was visible directly through the mesh, as opposed to the (currently) more common concrete deck.

Lead-based paint was removed from the bridge during a 2004 repainting effort and the steel grid deck was replaced in 2003. At this time, the bridge was expected to be replaced in the mid-2010s, and community meetings were held in 2007 to choose a design for the new span. However, the timetable to replace the bridge was accelerated as the condition of the 100-year-old piers deteriorated.

During the 2004 repainting, engineers discovered that the pier 3 bearings (east side of navigation channel) had displaced roughly 11 inches east of their original location as a result of unexpected movement of that pier (west) towards the main river channel. Hennepin County contracted with Wiss, Janey, Elstner and Associates (WJE) to investigate and report on the cause and extent of damage. The consultant's report concluded that evidence suggested the pier underwent many years, perhaps 50, of creep deflection due to sustained lateral earth pressure at the foundation which was held in check by the bearing assemblies. The bearing assemblies ultimate strength was finally overcome sometime in 2004 which allowed the unrestrained and rapid movement of the pier. The structural engineers at WJE were unable to predict the magnitude of future pier displacements.

Hennepin County, which owns and maintains the bridge, closed the bridge at 10:00 AM on April 25, 2008, due to safety concerns. Controlled explosions were used to demolish the bridge spans 14 months later on the morning of June 21, 2009.

Construction of the $80 million replacement bridge began early 2010 and was opened for traffic on October 27, 2012, at a cost of $104 million. The bridge includes a protected, shared-use path on both sides for pedestrians and bikes.

See also
List of crossings of the Upper Mississippi River

Joining were Bello Ibrahim (database administrator), Nafisa Yakubu (warehouse operations), Kabiru Musa (application developer), Aisha Danjuma (finance systems) and Sani Lawal from the vendor, Northstar Logistics Software.

Status Since Last Week

Bello reported that the full copy of the warehouse database, about 180 GB, was restored onto the new PostgreSQL server in the Kano data room on Monday. The initial load took eleven hours, longer than the six hours estimated, mainly because of large audit tables containing every barcode scan since 2019. Validation scripts showed matching row counts for all 84 tables, but checksum comparison flagged mismatches in three tables holding stock adjustment records.

Discussion of the Checksum Mismatches

Kabiru investigated and found that the old SQL Server database stores some quantity fields as floating point numbers, while the new schema uses fixed decimals. Rounding differences in values with many decimal places explain all the mismatches. After discussion, the group agreed on the following:

- Quantities will be stored with three decimal places, which matches how warehouse staff record weights in kilograms.
- Kabiru will write a script that reports any value where rounding changes the result by more than 0.001.
- Aisha will check whether finance reports depend on the unrounded values.
- No historical data will be modified without written sign-off from Nafisa as data owner.

Cutover Plan

Nafisa raised concern about the proposed cutover on the weekend of 29 April, because it coincides with the end-of-month stock count. Usman agreed that the risk was too high and the cutover was moved to the weekend of 13 May. Sani confirmed that the vendor can provide a support engineer on site for that weekend, though at an extra charge of USD 1,200.

Audit Table Archiving

To shorten future loads and keep the new database smaller, Bello proposed archiving scan records older than three years into a separate read-only database. Aisha pointed out that the tax authority may request records up to six years old. The group agreed to archive rather than delete, keeping the archive searchable through a simple reporting screen that Kabiru will build.

Testing

Warehouse supervisors will run user acceptance testing from 2 to 9 May, covering receiving, putaway, picking, dispatch and stock counts. Nafisa will select four supervisors from different shifts.

Actions

Kabiru to complete the rounding script by 17 April. Aisha to review finance dependencies by 19 April. Bello to prepare the archive database. Usman to confirm the vendor support booking and update the project calendar. Next sync on 19 April at the same time.

EduTrack Gradebook: Support for the 2025 Revised National Curriculum

EduTrack Gradebook is used by over 2,000 schools in Korea for recording assessment results and producing student reports. When the Ministry of Education introduced the 2022 revised national curriculum, phased in for middle and high schools from 2025, the assessment rules changed significantly. This documentation explains how EduTrack implements those changes and what teachers and administrators need to do.

Summary of Curriculum Changes Affecting Assessment

The revised curriculum introduces a high school credit system in which students choose more of their subjects, and assessment for many elective courses changes from relative ranking to absolute achievement levels. Five achievement levels, A to E, replace the old nine-grade relative scale in most subjects. Teachers must also record narrative descriptions of each student's competencies, known as detailed ability and characteristics notes, for every course.

How EduTrack Supports These Changes

* Course templates now include an assessment mode setting, either absolute achievement levels or relative grades, set by the school administrator for each course.
* Achievement level cut-offs default to 90, 80, 70 and 60 percent but can be adjusted within limits allowed by the provincial office of education.
* A narrative notes editor checks length limits and flags phrases that national guidelines discourage, such as references to parents' occupations.
* Credit tracking shows each student's accumulated credits and warns when a student risks falling short of the 192-credit graduation requirement.
* Reports can be exported in the format required by the National Education Information System.

Setting Up Courses

At the start of each semester, the school administrator should open Course Setup and confirm the assessment mode for each course. Minutes, Soil Fertility Research Group, Çukurova University, 2 September 2026

Attendees: Prof. Nurcan Özkan (chair), Dr. Emre Bulut, Dr. Sevgi Aksu, Hande Taş (PhD student), Volkan Er (laboratory manager). Minutes taken by Hande Taş.

Item 1: Nitrate Leaching Trial Results

Emre presented results from the second year of the lysimeter trial in the citrus orchard at the Adana research station. Average nitrate nitrogen in drainage water was 34 milligrams per litre under the farmer's standard practice of 300 kilograms of nitrogen per hectare, compared with 12 milligrams per litre under the split application of 180 kilograms guided by leaf analysis. Fruit yields did not differ significantly between treatments. Sevgi pointed out that the standard treatment exceeds the EU drinking water limit of 11.3 milligrams nitrate nitrogen per litre by a wide margin, which is relevant because many villages in the lower Seyhan basin still rely on shallow wells.

Item 2: Laboratory Capacity

Volkan reported that the autoanalyser for ammonium and nitrate has been unreliable since July and failed calibration three times last month. The service engineer from Istanbul can visit only in late October. Meanwhile, around 900 samples from the autumn sampling campaign will arrive in the next six weeks. The group discussed using the older distillation method as a backup, which is slower but reliable, or sending part of the samples to the Mersin regional laboratory.

Item 3: Thesis Progress

Hande summarised her work on phosphorus sorption in red Mediterranean soils. Sorption isotherms for twelve soils are complete, and she has found that soils with high iron oxide content retain phosphorus much more strongly than the calcareous soils of the plain, which was expected. Nurcan suggested adding a short incubation experiment to test whether organic amendments reduce sorption, since this would make the thesis more useful to growers.

Decisions

* Prepare a short policy brief on nitrate leaching for the provincial agriculture directorate, led by Emre, with a draft due by 30 September.
* Use the distillation method for urgent samples and send up to 300 samples to Mersin, with costs charged to the TÜBİTAK project budget.
* Add the organic amendment incubation to Hande's thesis plan, with Sevgi as co-supervisor for that chapter.
* Request a quote for a replacement autoanalyser, since repair costs have reached nearly half the price of a new unit.

Any Other Business

Nurcan reminded everyone that abstracts for the national soil science congress in Antalya are due on 15 October. At least two submissions from the group are expected, one on the leaching trial and one on phosphorus sorption.

Next meeting: 7 October, 10:00, seminar room 2.

She had a studio in Vaasa between 1866 and 1904. The first photographs of Vaasa is assumed to have been taken by her. She is known for her images of people in folk costumes from Österbotten, which were made into paintings by the artists Rudolf Åkerblom and Arvid Liljelund.

The Lemon Drop Kid is a 1934 American comedy drama film directed by Marshall Neilan and written by Howard J. Green, J.P. McEvoy and Damon Runyon. The film stars Lee Tracy, Helen Mack, William Frawley, Minna Gombell, Baby LeRoy, Kitty Kelly and Henry B. Walthall. The film was released on September 28,
1934, by Paramount Pictures. Plot Con artist and racetrack tout Wally Brooks hands a lemon drop to a man in a wheelchair, saying it will cure whatever ails him, then persuades the man, a millionaire named Griggsby, to bet $100 on a horse. Wally knows this horse can't win and intends to pocket the cash. The horse does win, so Wally and his partner Dunhill, alias "The Professor," take it on the lam.

Lying low in an out-of-the-way place, Wally meets town drunk Jonas Deering and his beautiful daughter Alice. A love affair blossoms and they marry, but when Alice is about to give birth and having serious medical problems, Wally needs money so he robs Mr. Potter, her boss. Alice dies in childbirth. A despondent Wally shuns his own son, Wally Jr., and isn't sure where to turn next. The Professor marries longtime girlfriend Maizie and offers to raise Wally Jr., and even better, Griggsby shows up, claiming the lemon drop did help his arthritis. He volunteers to become Wally Jr.'s legal guardian and gives Wally some money, minus what the bet on his horse would have won. 2 Related Work and Hypotheses Opening choice in competitive chess has been studied mainly through large databases of elite games, where researchers ask which openings score best for White or how opening fashions spread among top players. Much less attention has been paid to how opening choice
relates to player development at sub-elite levels. This paper addresses that gap using data from the All India FIDE Rating Open tournaments held between 2015 and 2024, which together include about 412,000 rated games played by more than 58,000 Indian players. 2.1 Previous Studies

Early quantitative work on chess openings by Ribeiro and colleagues showed that opening popularity follows a heavy-tailed distribution, with a small number of openings accounting for most games. Later studies using online platforms found that players under 1600 rarely deviate from a narrow set of openings learned early, and that switching openings is associated with temporary drops in performance. However, online games differ from over-the-board tournaments in time controls and stakes, so their findings may not transfer directly.

In the Indian context, Venkatraman and Pillai examined junior players at national championships between 2008 and 2016 and found that juniors coached at academies in Chennai and Kolkata were more likely to play mainstream openings such as the Ruy Lopez and the Sicilian Najdorf, while players from regions with fewer coaching opportunities more often used offbeat systems. They did not, 
however, link opening choice to subsequent rating progress. 2.2 Hypotheses

Building on these studies, we test four hypotheses: 1. Players who adopt mainstream openings with both colours before reaching a rating of 1600 show faster rating
 gains over the following three years. 2. The association in the first hypothesis is weaker for players who also play many classical games per year, since practice may substitute for opening knowledge. 
3. Players who frequently switch openings, defined as changing their main reply to 1.e4 more than twice in two years, show slower rating gains than stable players. 4. Players from districts without registered chess academies benefit more from adopting mainstream openings than players from districts with academies. 2.3 Theoretical Rationale The first hypothesis rests on the idea that mainstream openings lead to positions rich in instructive plans and well covered by published material, giving improving players more opportunities to learn. The third hypothesis draws on research on skill acquisition suggesting that consolidation within a stable domain supports progress better than frequent switching. The fourth reflects the possibility that mainstream openings partly compensate for limited access to coaches, because so much free instructional material on them exists in books and videos. Section 3 describes the dataset and the construction of variables used to test these hypotheses, including our method for classifying openings using the ECO codes recorded in tournament files submitted by organisers to the All India Chess Federation.

Feasibility Study: Moving the Municipal GIS Database of Ústí nad Labem to PostGIS

Prepared for the IT department of the Statutory City of Ústí nad Labem by Geodata Sever s.r.o.
Authors: Ing. Kryštof Mach and Mgr. Eliška Rybářová. Delivered 30 January 2026. 1 Introduction The city maintains its geographic information system on an ArcGIS Enterprise platform with an Oracle 19c geodatabase. The system holds around 140 layers, including the city's technical map, land ownership parcels, street lighting, green areas, waste collection points and planning documentation. Licence and support costs for the 
current platform have risen by about 40 percent over three years, reaching 2.3 million CZK annually, and the Oracle server reaches end of support in 2027. The city asked us to assess whether the geodatabase could be moved to PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension, and at what cost and risk. 2 Current State We inventoried all layers, their schemas, their editing workflows and the 
applications that consume them. The analysis found the following:

- 112 layers are simple feature classes that can be migrated with standard tools without loss of information. - 19 layers use Esri-specific features, mainly versioning and topology rules, that have no direct equivalent in PostGIS.
- 9 layers belong to the technical map of the city and are edited daily by four surveyors in the department
 of land registry. - Seven internal applications and the public map portal read directly from the geodatabase, three of them through proprietary connectors. 3 Assessment

Migration of the 112 simple layers is low risk and could be completed in about two months, including validation. The 19 layers with versioning and topology require redesign: versioning can be replaced by a history table with triggers, and topology rules by database constraints and periodic validation queries, but editing workflows will change and surveyors will need training. The public map portal can be switched to GeoServer reading from 
PostGIS, which the city already uses for its open data services. The most significant risk concerns the technical map. Its editing workflow depends on long-running versioned edits that are reconciled at the end of each survey job, and replacing this with a different model needs careful testing
to avoid conflicting edits.

4 Costs We estimate one-off migration costs of 3.4 million CZK, including redesign, application changes, training and a six-month parallel run. Annual operating costs after migration would fall to about 0.9 million CZK, mainly for support and hosting
, giving a payback period of roughly two and a half years. 5 Recommendation We recommend a phased migration, starting with the simple layers and the public portal

 in 2026, and moving the technical map only in 2027 after
a pilot with one surveyor. The city should keep the
ArcGIS desktop licences for the surveyors during the transition.

- 9 layers belong to the technical map of the city and are edited daily by four surveyors in the department of land registry.
- Seven internal applications and the public map portal read directly from the geodatabase, three of them through proprietary connectors.

3 Assessment

Migration of the 112 simple layers is low risk and could be completed in about two months, including validation. The 19 layers with versioning and topology require redesign: versioning can be replaced by a history table with triggers, and topology rules by database constraints and periodic validation queries, but editing workflows will change and surveyors will need training. Bola Are (born 1 October 1954) is a Nigerian gospel singer and former President of the Gospel Musicians Association of Nigeria.

Early life
She was born on 1 October 1954 in Erio a town in Ekiti-West local government, of Ekiti State, southwestern Nigeria to the Elder Babayomi and Mrs T. A. Babayomi who hail from Erio, Ekiti State, Nigeria. She was brought up by four major prophets in Christ Apostolic Church - Apostle Ayodele Babalola, Prophet Babajide, Prophet Akande and Prophet T.O. Obadare. She spent most of her time on the mountain and receives her inspiration from holy spirit.

Education
Are began her primary education at Christ Apostolic Church (CAC) Primary school in her home town and her secondary education at Christ Apostolic Church Grammar School at Efon Alaye in Ekiti State before she proceeded to The Polytechnic, Ibadan where she obtained a diploma certificate in accounting. In July 1985, she was awarded an honorary doctorate degree in Music at St. John's University.

Personal life
Bola Are got married in 1977 to the late Pastor J.O Are and are blessed with children. Her children are singers and musicians. Bola Are Gospel foundation international aimed at catering for the needs of the less privileged in Nigeria, it was founded in 1995.Her recording studio, school of Gospel Music International was founded on 7 July 1990, to give gospel musicians a platform that would lead them in the way of the Lord. The school is currently located at C .A .C Agbala Oluwa, Bola Are street Ogbere Idi- Obi, beside Airport Quarters Ibadan, Bola Are Okiki Jesu Records international. Bola Are marked her 40 years on stage on 5 October 2013.

Career
Are started singing from the age of two, she knew she would serve the Lord at a very young age and pursued it. Her parents told her that she started singing a few day before her first birthday, that made her considers herself a born singer. However, after deciding to follow her passion for ministry, Evangelist Bola Are started a music band called Bola and Her Spiritual Singers on 26 June 1973. In August 1977, she released her first musical album Baba Ku Ise. As at 2014, Are had released over seventy albums.

Albums (1965–2000)
Divine Praise of the King Of Kings – 1965
Ajaga Babiloni Wooo – 1967
Anointed Praise 2 – 1970
Bola Are Live – 1971
Agbara Esu Ko Da Nibiti Jesu Gbe Njoba – 1971
Homage 1 – 1974
Halleluyah Jesus Lives – 1974
Adura Owuro – 1977
Baba Kuse – 1977
Anointed Praise 1 – 1979
Jesus Is Coming Back, Be Ready! – 1981
Bibo Jesu Leekeji – 1988
Gbongbo Idile Jesse – 1991
Homage 2 (Tribute To Apostle T.O Obadare) – 1995
Lion Of Judah – 1995
Oore Ofe – 1998
Power In Praise – 2000
Apostle Joseph Ayodele Babalola – 2000

See also
List of Nigerian gospel musicians

Reading a Reef Transect: A Beginner's Walkthrough

If you have joined the Galway Marine Volunteers for their autumn trip to the Red Sea, you will spend most of your dive time running belt transects across the fringing reef near Dahab. The method sounds technical, but it comes down to swimming slowly along a measuring tape and writing down what lies beneath it. This tutorial walks through a single survey from kitting up to entering your numbers in the evening spreadsheet.

Before You Enter the Water

Check that your slate has the coded category sheet clipped to it, that your pencil is tied on with a short cord, and that your buddy carries the 50-metre fibreglass tape. Agree on a depth before descending; our team uses 8 metres on the reef crest and 14 metres on the slope. Ciaran Moloney, who leads the dives, will hand each pair a laminated card showing the twelve benthic categories we record, from hard coral and soft coral to rubble, sand and turf algae.

Running the Transect

Once you reach the agreed depth, follow this sequence without rushing:

1. Fix the tape's zero end to a dead coral head or rock, never to living tissue.
2. Let your buddy swim the tape out along the depth contour while you hover a metre above it.
3. Starting at zero, look straight down at every half-metre mark and note the category directly under the tape.
4. Record fish counts separately, only for the five indicator species on the back of your card.
5. Reel the tape back in carefully so it does not snag on branching Acropora colonies.

Making Sense of the Numbers

Back at the dive centre, each pair enters 100 points per transect into the shared sheet that Fionnuala Gallagher maintains. Percentage cover is simply the count for a category divided by the total points and multiplied by one hundred. If you counted 37 hard coral points, the hard coral cover on that line is 37 percent, which for this stretch of coast would be fairly healthy.

Do not worry if your first transect disagrees with your buddy's by a few points. Calibration improves quickly, and on day three we run a paired comparison on the same tape so that everyone can see where their identifications drift. Bleached colonies still count as hard coral, but tick the small bleaching box beside the entry so the trend can be tracked across seasons.

Common Mistakes

The most frequent error is drifting upwards as you concentrate, which widens your view and inflates the count of conspicuous colonies. Another is skipping points that fall on awkward overhangs. Record every point, even when the answer is simply shadow or unknown, and the dataset will stay honest.

The Book of Alma: The Son of Alma (), usually referred to as the Book of Alma, is one of the books that make up the Book of Mormon. The title refers to Alma the Younger, a prophet and "chief judge" of the Nephites. Alma is the longest book in the Book of Mormon and consists of sixty-three chapters, taking up almost a third of the volume.

Narrative

Historical outline
The Book of Alma is the longest of all the books of the Book of Mormon, consisting of 63 chapters. The book records the first 39 years of what the Nephites termed "the reign of the judges", a period in which the Nephite nation adopted a constitutional theocratic government in which the judicial and executive branches of the government were combined.

The history of the book is outlined as follows:

Challenges to the beginning of the republic
The first four chapters describe the rebellions of followers of Nehor and Amlici. Contrary to the dominant lay ministry that existed in the Nephite culture, Nehor established a church that taught universal salvation in which priests were given separate social status and were paid for their ministry. After killing a religious leader during a theological argument, Nehor was tried and executed for his crimes. The followers of Amlici resented the dominant political and religious parties and sought to reestablish the monarchy that the reign of the judges had replaced. Alma, who was chief judge, governor, and high priest over the people of Nephi, led an army against Amlici and his followers and drove the rebellion out of the land.

Ministry of Alma among the Nephites
Towards the end of chapter four, Alma realizes that the affairs of the Church require his entire concentration. He resigns from his political office and appoints Nephihah as chief judge and governor of the land. Chapters 5–16 record sermons and missionary travels of Alma between 83 and 78 BC. Alma and one of his converted followers, Amulek, provide important teachings about the atonement of Christ, overcoming pride and the natural man, retaining conversion, the resurrection of all men, and judgment day. Later, their teachings about faith and worship in Alma 32-34 are important sources of instruction and insight.

Ministry of the sons of Mosiah among the Lamanites
Chapters 17 to 27 describe the missionary labors of the sons of King Mosiah II who was the last king over the people of Nephi before the peaceful transition of the nation from a monarchy to a republican form of government. The sons of Mosiah, named Ammon, Aaron, Omner and Himni, chose to devote themselves to missionary labors preaching to the people of the Lamanite nation, which periodically went to war against the Nephite nation. They lived and taught among the Lamanites between the years 91 and 77 BC.

Ministry of Alma among the Zoramites
Chapters 28 to 35 relate the account of a rebellion of a subgroup of the Nephite nation, who called themselves Zoramites. The Zoramites believed in a form of predestination and taught that all others except their people would be damned. Their apostasy from the Church was conspiring against the plans to rebel against the Nephite government. Alma took two of his sons, the sons of Mosiah, Amulek, and Zeezrom on a mission among the Zoramites in an attempt to restore their loyalty to both the Church and the state. Alma and his companions had some success among the poor class of Zoramites who were then exiled from the Zoramite community by the governing rich class of Zoramites. The wealthier Zoramites eventually defected and united with the Lamanites.

Commandments of Alma to his children
Chapters 36 to 42 record the teachings of Alma to his sons, Helaman, Shiblon, and Corianton. These teachings discuss the ministry and atonement of Jesus, the laws of justice and mercy, the need for repentance, and the resurrection and judgment of all people.

Andrew Graham Salter (born 1 June 1993) is a Welsh cricketer. Salter is a right-handed batsman who bowls right-arm off break. He was born at Haverfordwest, Pembrokeshire, and was educated at Milford Haven School.

Salter made his debut in county cricket for Wales Minor Counties against Wiltshire in the 2010 MCCA Knockout Trophy, and in that same season he made his debut in the Minor Counties Championship against Devon. In early 2011, he played four Youth One Day Internationals for England Under-19s against Sri Lanka Under-19s during England Under-19s tour there. While studying for a Higher National Diploma in Sport Coaching & Development at Cardiff Metropolitan University, Salter made his first-class debut for Cardiff MCC University in the team's inaugural appearance in first-class cricket against Somerset at Taunton Vale Sports Club Ground in 2012. He featured in a second first-class appearance in that season for Cardiff MCCU against Warwickshire at Edgbaston. He made his debut in county cricket for Glamorgan in a List A match against Durham in the 2012 Clydesdale Bank 40, making a further appearance in that competition against Nottinghamshire. Salter managed to take a wicket with his very first career ball in the County Championship when he had Leicestershire's Shiv Thakor caught behind. In April 2022, in the opening round of matches in the 2022 County Championship, Salter took his maiden five-wicket haul in first-class cricket, with 7 for 45 against Durham.

Production Trial Report: Reducing Crumb Defects in Industrial Rye-Wheat Bread

Prepared by the quality department of Piekarnia Zagłoba S.A., Częstochowa plant. Authors: Monika Żak (quality manager) and Krystian Bielecki (process technologist). Trial period: 6 January to 14 February 2027.

Purpose

During the second half of 2026, customer complaints about the company's best-selling product, a 600-gram mixed rye-wheat loaf sold under the name Chleb Wiejski, rose from an average of 12 to 41 per month. Most complaints concerned a gummy, dense layer near the bottom of the loaf and large holes under the crust. This report describes a series of production trials designed to identify and correct the causes.

Background

The loaf is made with 60 percent wheat flour type 750 and 40 percent rye flour type 720, using a rye sourdough produced in a continuous fermenter. Dough is mixed in batches of 300 kilograms, divided, proofed in a tunnel prover for 55 minutes, and baked for 38 minutes in a tunnel oven. In September 2026 the plant switched rye flour supplier after the previous mill closed.

Hypotheses

Initial analysis of production records suggested several possible causes. The new rye flour showed a falling number of 128 seconds, compared with around 180 seconds for the previous supplier, indicating higher amylase activity. Sourdough acidity had also drifted lower, and the prover had been running slightly warmer after a sensor replacement in October.

Trial Design

Four trials were run on the production line, each over three days, changing one factor at a time:

1. Restoring prover temperature from 38 to the original specification of 34 degrees Celsius.
2. Increasing sourdough share to raise dough acidity from pH 4.6 to 4.3.
3. Blending the new rye flour with 30 percent rye flour from a second supplier with a higher falling number.
4. Combining all three changes.

Samples from each trial were evaluated by a trained panel of six staff and measured with a texture analyser at 24 hours after baking.

Results

Correcting prover temperature reduced large holes under the crust noticeably, but had little effect on the gummy layer. Increasing acidity improved crumb firmness and reduced gumminess by about a third. Blending flours had the largest single effect on gumminess. The combined trial produced loaves that the panel could not distinguish from retained samples made in early 2026, and texture measurements were within the historical range.

Discussion

The findings are consistent with what is known about rye baking: high amylase activity breaks down starch during baking, especially if acidity is not sufficient to suppress the enzyme, leading to a sticky crumb. The warmer prover allowed over-proofing, which explains the holes.

Recommendations

The plant should adopt the combined changes as standard. Falling number should be added to incoming flour specifications, with a minimum of 160 seconds for rye flour, and checked for every delivery. The prover temperature sensor should be included in the monthly calibration schedule. Complaint numbers will be reviewed again at the end of April.
