Loga Ramin Torkian ()،(Born: September 23 ،1964) is a musician and the co-founder of the groups Axiom of Choice and Niyaz. Both groups incorporate Persian and Middle Eastern themes into their music. Torkian composes music and plays
 several instruments, including the Iranian tar, the Turkish saz, and the GuitarViol, an electric guitar-like instrument that uses a bow and is adapted from a 14th-century instrument. Several of the lyrics in his songs draw on or include traditional Middle-Eastern prayers, songs or chants. His music has also appeared in several films, such as The Chosen One (1995), America So Beautiful (2001), Plastic Flowers Never Die (2008), and Crossing Over (2009). Personal life

He is married to singer Azam Ali and they have one son. He previously was married to Yatrikadevi Shah-Rais and was co-owner of the

026 This log records changes to the field protocol for the provincial Japanese encephalitis catch-up campaign targeting children aged one to twelve and adult farm workers in rural counties. It is maintained by the provincial infectious disease control team. Each change lists what was altered, when, and the 
reasoning. Revision 4, 10 September 2026 • Extended the adult target group to include seaso
nal workers on pig farms and rice paddies regardless of nationality or residence 
status. • Added Vietnamese, Khmer and Nepali versions of the screening questionnaire. • Moved evening vaccination sessions at community halls from 19:00 to 18:00. The extension to seasonal workers reflects data from the provincial health and environment research institute, which found that 70 percent of mosquito pools collected near pig farms in Gimhae and Miryang tested positive for the virus in August, and that many of the people working nearest those farms were foreign seasonal workers who had not been reached in earlier rounds. Translations were reviewed by community interpreters, including Ms. Doan Thi Kim Oanh of the Gimhae Multicultural Family Support Center. Sessions moved earlier because mosquito biting peaks at dusk, and staff were concerned about vaccinating people outdoors at that time. Revision 3, 4 July 2026

• Replaced the two-dose inactivated vaccine schedule for adults with a single dose of the live attenuated vaccine, except for pregnant women and immunocompromi
sed people. • Allowed vaccination at farm sites rather than requiring workers to visit health centres.

The schedule change followed national guidan
ce from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency issued in June. A single dose simplifies follow-up, which had been the main weakness of the campaign, since only 46 pe
rcent of adults who received a first dose returned for the second. Farm-site vaccination was requested by farm owners, including Mr. Chun Byung-ok in Hapcheon, who said workers could not leave during harvest without losing wages. Revision 2, 15 May 2026 • Corrected the minimum interval between doses for children from three weeks to seven days for the first two doses, as stated in the vaccine product information. • Added a requirement to record lot numbers for every dose in the electronic registry. The interval correction fixed a transcription error in the original protocol, which had delayed some children's second doses unnecessarily. 

Lot number recording wa
s added after a supplier recall elsewhere in Korea showed that several counties could not identify which children had received doses from
 the affected lot. Revision 1, 1 April 2026 • Initial protocol issued for the campaign, covering children in eight rural counties.

Contact Questions about the protocol should be directed to the campaign coordinator, Dr. Nam Ji-hye, at the provincial public health division in Changwon.

HPV School Vaccination Programme, Coordinator Guide

This page is for school nurses and district coordinators in the ASL Città di Torino working on the human papillomavirus programme for pupils in the second year of lower secondary school. Last reviewed by Dr Michela Rota on 15 September 2026.

Overview

Since 2024 the ASL has offered HPV vaccination in schools rather than only at vaccination centres, because coverage among twelve-year-olds had stalled at around 58 percent for girls and 41 percent for boys. The school-based approach raised coverage to 72 and 63 percent respectively in its first year. For 2026-2027 the programme covers 124 schools and roughly 8,900 pupils, with two doses given six months apart.

Annual Timeline

September and October are for consent, November to January for first doses, and April to June for second doses. Coordinators should not schedule sessions in the two weeks before Christmas or during school trips, since attendance drops sharply and rescheduling consumes a lot of nurse time.

Consent Procedure

Parents receive an information letter and consent form through the school's electronic register. Paper forms remain available for families without access. Remember the following points:

- Both parents should sign if both exercise parental responsibility, but one signature is accepted when the form says the other parent agrees
- Pupils who are fourteen or older at the time of vaccination may express their own view, which must be recorded
- Consent is valid for both doses unless withdrawn in writing
- Forms received after the session date are still accepted, and the pupil is offered a catch-up slot

Running a Session

Each session needs two nurses and one doctor present in the building, a private room for vaccination, and a separate room where pupils sit for fifteen minutes afterwards. Fainting is the most common reaction in this age group, so pupils should be seated, not standing, when vaccinated. Teachers should not be asked to supervise the observation room alone. Record each dose on the tablet before the pupil leaves; entries sync to the regional registry when the device next connects to the network.

Talking to Hesitant Families

Many parents who decline have specific worries rather than general opposition. The most frequent questions concern why boys are vaccinated, whether the vaccine encourages early sexual activity, and how safety is monitored. HPV School Vaccination Programme, Coordinator Guide

This page is for school nurses and district coordinators in the ASL Città di Torino working on the human papillomavirus programme for pupils in the second year of lower secondary school. Last reviewed by Dr Michela Rota on 15 September 2026.

Overview

Since 2024 the ASL has offered HPV vaccination in schools rather than only at vaccination centres, because coverage among twelve-year-olds had stalled at around 58 percent for girls and 41 percent for boys. The school-based approach raised coverage to 72 and 63 percent respectively in its first year. For 2026-2027 the programme covers 124 schools and roughly 8,900 pupils, with two doses given six months apart.

Annual Timeline

September and October are for consent, November to January for first doses, and April to June for second doses. Coordinators should not schedule sessions in the two weeks before Christmas or during school trips, since attendance drops sharply and rescheduling consumes a lot of nurse time.

Consent Procedure

Parents receive an information letter and consent form through the school's electronic register. Paper forms remain available for families without access. Remember the following points:

- Both parents should sign if both exercise parental responsibility, but one signature is accepted when the form says the other parent agrees
- Pupils who are fourteen or older at the time of vaccination may express their own view, which must be recorded
- Consent is valid for both doses unless withdrawn in writing
- Forms received after the session date are still accepted, and the pupil is offered a catch-up slot

Running a Session

Each session needs two nurses and one doctor present in the building, a private room for vaccination, and a separate room where pupils sit for fifteen minutes afterwards. Fainting is the most common reaction in this age group, so pupils should be seated, not standing, when vaccinated. Teachers should not be asked to supervise the observation room alone. Record each dose on the tablet before the pupil leaves; entries sync to the regional registry when the device next connects to the network.

Talking to Hesitant Families

Many parents who decline have specific worries rather than general opposition. The most frequent questions concern why boys are vaccinated, whether the vaccine encourages early sexual activity, and how safety is monitored. Short answers to each are available in the FAQ document linked from the programme folder. When a parent wants to discuss further, offer a call with the programme doctor instead of debating at the school gate.

Tahc'a Okute Wakpa is a stream in Oglala Lakota County, South Dakota, in the United States.

In the Lakota language, tahc'a okute means "deer-hunting grounds" and wakpa means a stream or river.

The stream was previously known as Squaw-Humper Creek, reputedly named for a local white man who had a live-in Native American girlfriend (squaw). The term "squaw-humper" was cited as "contemptuous" as early as 1940, and was removed from federal usage by a decision of the Board on Geographic Names in 2015. See also
Squaw Humper Dam List of rivers of South Dakota

Software Engineering Practice, Lecture 12: Releasing a Mobile App Safely Lecturer: Dr. Shiori Takamatsu, School of Computing, Tokyo Metropolitan Institute. Notes written by tutor Genki Hasegawa for students who missed Thursday's session. The lecture began with a story from Dr. Takamatsu's time at a ride-hailing company in 2021. A release containing a small change to the payment screen went to all Android users at once on a Friday evening. A bug affected only one older phone model popular among drivers, but that was enough to prevent thousands of drivers from accepting fares over a busy weekend. Her point was that mobile releases differ from web releases in one important way: once an app version is on a user's phone, you cannot simply roll it back. Why Mobile Releases Are Different

On the web, a bad deployment can be reverted on the server in minutes. On mobile, each release passes through an app store review, users update at their own pace, and old versions remain in use for months. This means release practices must focus on catching problems before full exposure and on controlling features from the server. Practices Covered * Staged rollouts, releasing first to a small percentage of users and watching metrics before expanding * Feature flags that let teams switch features on or off without a new release
* Minimum supported version checks that can prompt or force users to update * Crash reporting and analytics configured before release, not after problems appear * Release trains with fixed schedules so that no single release carries too much change Metrics to Watch During Rollout

Dr
. Takamatsu emphasised watching crash-free session rates, the success rate of the app's most important action, and the volume and content of user reviews. She recommended defining thresholds before the rollout starts, so the decision to pause is mechanical rather than emotional. Teams under pressure to ship tend to explain away early warning signs. Store Review Considerations The lecture briefly covered app store review. Reviews can take anything from a few hours to several days, and rejections often concer
n privacy disclosures, in-app purchase rules or incomplete metadata. Planning releases with buffer time for review avoids last-minute pressure to cut corners.

Assignment The group assignment for the next two weeks is to write a release plan for the course's sample app, Hanami, including rollout stages, metrics with thresholds, and a feature flag strategy for the new photo sharing feature. Plans must be submitted through the learning portal by 16 October. Office hours are on Tuesday from 15:00 in room 6-402.

The steel-string acoustic guitar is a modern form of guitar that descends from the gut-strung Romantic guitar, but is strung with steel strings for a brighter, louder sound. Like the modern classical guitar, it is often referred to simply as an acoustic guitar, or sometimes as a folk guitar. The most common type is often called a flat top guitar, to distinguis
h it from the more sp
ecialized archtop guitar and other variations. The standard tuning for an acoustic guitar is E-A-D-G-B-E (low to high), although many players, particularly fingerpickers, use alternate tunings (scordatura), such as open 
G (D-G-D-G-B-D), open D (D-A-D-F-A-D), drop D (D-A-D-G-B-E), or D-A-D-G-A-D (particularly in Irish traditional music).

Construction Steel-string guitars vary in construction and materials. Different woods and approach to bracing affect the instrument's timbre or tone. While there is little scientif
ic evidence, many players and luthiers believe a well-made guitar's tone improves over time. They theorize that a decrease in the content of hemicellulose, crystallization
of cellulose, and changes to lignin over time all result in its wood gaining better resonating properties. Types
Steel-string acoustic guitars are commonly constructed in several body types, varying in size, depth, and proportion. In general, the guitar's soundbox can be thought of as composed of two mating chambers: the upper bouts (a bout being the rounded corner of an instrument body) on the neck end of the body, and lower bouts 
(on the bridge end). These meet at the waist, or the narrowest part of the body face near the soundhole. The proportion and overall size of these two parts helps determine the overall tonal balance and "native sound" of a particular body style – the larger the body, the louder the volume.

The Russian
 Eastern Okraina () was a local government that existed in the Russian Far East region in 1920 during the Russian Civil War of 1917–1923. History
In 1919, White forces in Western Siberia were defeated by the Bolsheviks. On 4 January 1920, the Supreme Ruler of Russia, Alexander Kolchak, issued an order transferring to ataman Grigory Semyonov "the whole civil and military power on the territory of Russia eastern outskirts".

Based on this order, on 16 January 1920, Grigory Semyonov announced in Chita the creation of the "Government of the Russian Eastern Outskirts", with Sergey Taskin as its head. Semyonov's actions were supported by the commanders of Japanese troops in Siberia. On 6 April 1920, a hastily convened Constituent Assembly gathered at Verkhneudinsk and proclaimed the establishment of a separate administration: the Far Eastern Republic (FER). On May 14, Japanese commanders agreed to talk w

ith the Bolshevik-oriented FER, and on May 24 negotiations began at Railway Station, 125 Kilometers west of Chita. The Japanese insisted that the Government of the Russian Eastern Outskirts should be an equal party during the negotiations for the creation of a united Far East government, but the FER disagreed, and negotiations were stopped in early June. On July 3, 1920, Japan issued a proclamation about evacuating Japanese troops from Siberia. Semyonov understood that he could not survive without Japanese support. He asked the Japanese government to delay the evacuation for four months, and tried to negotiate a merger with the Government of Zemstvo of Maritime Territory, but unsuccessfully. The Gongota negotiations resumed on July 10, 1920, and on July 17 the FER representatives and Japanese military officials in Siberia signed the Gongota Agreement. The agreed terms provided for Japanese evacuation from the Transbaikal and the establishment of a neutral border zone between the territories of the parties. The Whites understood that they could not stop the Reds without Japanese support, and began to retreat to the southeast, preparing to retreat into Chinese territory. Only small White military forces still held Chita, blocking the Trans-Siberia Railway
. In September 1920, a was organized under Semyonov's auspices, and Semyonov transferred his civil powers to it. At the same time military forces of the FER, masked as independent groups of partisans, began to move through the neutral zone towards Chita; on September 15, an assembly of workers 
of the Eastern Transbaikal Region in Nerchinsk proclaimed the creation of a Regional Revolution committee for the eastern Transbaikal. On October 15, Japanese troops left Chita, and the Reds demanded the capitulation of the Whites' garrison there. The Whites declined, and on October 19 the Reds began to advance on Chita, which they captured on October 22. On October 25 the government of the FER moved from Verkhneudinsk to Chita. At the end of October, the Provisional Eastern-Transbaikal Assembly, during a joint session with the Nerchinsk Regional Revolution Committee, declared its own dissolution, and three Far Eastern pro-Soviet governments joined in the united FER. The Eastern Okraina, left without territory, collapsed, and Semyonov and his remaining troops went into exile in Chinese territory.

Lucretia Johansdotter Gyllenhielm (1561–1585), was the illegitimate daughter of John III of Sweden and Karin Hansdotter. She was reportedly the favorite of her father.

Biography
Lucretia Gyllenhielm and her siblings were ennobled and granted the surname Gyllenhielm in 1577, though she and her sister often used only their patronymic. Lucretia was the favorite of her father. She was betrothed to the nobleman Karl Gustafsson Stenbock. When she died unmarried in 1585 at the age of 24, her father the king became distraught and issued an investigation if she had died as the result of witchcraft. Karl Gustafsson Stenbock accused the noblewoman Kerstin Gabrielsdotter Ulfsax, wife of Joen Nilsson (1536-1600). She was rumored to have murdered her late spouse and of having bewitched Lucretia. Ulfsax was arrested, and after having failed to collect twelve female nobles as character witnesses, she was executed.

Notes from the opening preparation session for the Nagpur team ahead of the National Team Chess Championship, held on 28 September 2026 at the Vidarbha Chess Association hall, Dharampeth. Present: GM Rahul Wankhede (team captain), IM Swapnil Dhopade, FM Aniket Bawankar, WIM Pranali Gajbhiye, Ketan Bhoyar (second), and coach Mukund Deshmukh.

Purpose of the Session

Mukund explained that the championship in Hyderabad starts on 12 October with nine rounds over eight days. Opponents are known only on the evening before each round, so preparation must focus on broad repertoire choices rather than specific players. The aim of the session was to agree which openings each board will play and to divide the work of updating files.

Review of Last Year

Rahul reminded the group that the team lost two matches last year largely because of opening problems on the lower boards. In the round against Tamil Nadu, Pranali reached a passive position against the Catalan and lost after a long defence. Aniket was surprised by a sideline in the Najdorf and spent forty minutes on the clock by move fifteen. Both agreed that their repertoires had become too broad and that depth mattered more than variety.

Repertoire Decisions

After discussion, the boards agreed on the following core choices:

1. Board one, Rahul, will stick with 1.e4 and the Ruy Lopez with white, and the Grünfeld against 1.d4.
2. Board two, Swapnil, will play 1.d4 with the Catalan and, as black, the Caro-Kann against 1.e4.
3. Board three, Aniket, will keep the Najdorf but prepare the 6.h3 and 6.Bg5 lines in particular depth.
4. Board four, Pranali, will switch from the Queen's Indian to the Ragozin against 1.d4, which offers more active play.
5. The reserve, Ketan, will cover the English Opening for the team and prepare quick summaries for any board that faces it.

Division of Work

Ketan will maintain the shared opening files and update them each evening during the tournament based on the next day's pairings. Swapnil will prepare a document on the Catalan structures for Pranali, since her new Ragozin choice often meets similar ideas. Mukund will arrange two training matches against Pune players on 4 and 5 October to test the new lines under tournament conditions.

Other Matters

The team discussed physical preparation and agreed to walk together for thirty minutes each morning in Hyderabad before the round. Rahul asked everyone to avoid late-night blitz online during the event.

Next Session

The group meets again on 6 October to review the training matches and finalise files before travelling to Hyderabad on 10 October.

Launch campaign log for FlandersSat-1, maintained by the integration team at Spacebel Liège and the satellite operations group in Redu. Each entry records a change to the launch plan or the flight configuration and explains why it was made. Entries appear in reverse chronological order.

Revision F, 28 August

- Launch date moved from 9 September to 16 September
- Fill level of the cold gas propulsion tank reduced from 92 to 88 percent
- Final battery charge rescheduled to 36 hours before launch instead of 48

The launch provider postponed the mission by one week after an anomaly on a previous flight of the same vehicle, which is still under investigation. Our satellite is not affected directly, but the delay meant that the propellant tank would remain sealed and pressurised for longer than planned. To keep the tank pressure within the qualified range during the extra days in the hot fairing environment, we reduced the fill level slightly. The loss of propellant reduces the orbit-keeping margin from nine years to just over eight, which remains well above the mission requirement of five years. The battery charge was moved later so that the satellite starts its mission with the highest possible state of charge despite the longer wait.

Revision E, 12 August

- Antenna deployment timer changed from 30 to 45 minutes after separation
- Added a second beacon frequency for the first week of operations

The team led by Céline Dumont analysed the separation sequence again after the provider revised its predicted tip-off rates. A longer delay before antenna deployment gives the satellite more time to stabilise, reducing the risk that an antenna hits the structure. The second beacon frequency was requested by the ground station in Kiruna, which experienced interference on our primary frequency during compatibility tests.

Revision D, 30 July

- Shipment from Liège to the launch site moved forward by four days
- Customs documentation updated with the new dual-use classification

The shipping change followed advice from the freight forwarder that port congestion could delay the container. Arriving earlier gives the team, coordinated on site by Lucas Verheyen, a buffer before the start of the launch campaign. The customs update was needed because the Belgian export control office reclassified the star tracker, which required a new licence. The licence was granted on 24 July.

Outlook

The next revision is expected after the final readiness review on 10 September. Any further change to the launch date will be posted here within one working day of confirmation by the launch provider.

Diagnosing Gear Shifting Problems Wiki page for volunteer mechanics at the Pedálpont community bike workshop, Budapest District VIII. Owner: Márton Kerekes. Read this before working on a customer's derailleur, especially if you are in your first three months of volunteering. Most bikes brought to Pedálpont with "gears not working" have a cable or adjustment problem, not a broken part. Our records for 2024 show that of 318 shifting complaints, only 41 needed a new derailleur or shifter. Volunteers who start replacing parts before diagnosing the cause waste the customer's money and our limited stock of second-hand components, so please follow the order of checks below. Order of Checks • Look at the derailleur hanger from behind the bike; a bent hanger makes everything else impossible to adjust. • Shift through all gears on a stand and note exactly where 
the ch
ain hesitates, skips or overshoots. • Check the cable for fraying at the shifter and the clamp bolt, and for rust insid
e the housing. • Test barrel adjuster tension in half-turn steps. • Confirm the limit screws stop the chain from falling off at either end of 

the cassette. • Inspect chain wear with the gauge; a stretched chain skips under load even if the shifting is perfect. Common Causes and Fixes If
 the chain hesitates when shifting to larger cogs, cable tension is usually too low; turn the barrel adjuster anticlockwise half a turn and retest. If it hesitates when shifting to smaller cogs, tension is too high. If shifting is sluggish in both directions and the lever feels stiff, the cable or housing is dirty or corroded and should be replaced, which costs 
the customer about 1,500 forints for a cable and housing from our stock. A bent hanger is the most underestimated problem. Many bikes arrive after being laid on the ground on their right side, especially those parked at the Corvin-negyed racks. Use the hanger alignment tool on the blue wall board, and remember that aluminium hangers can crack if bent back too far. We keep replacement hangers for the most common frames in drawer 14. When to Ask for Help Ask a senior volunteer before replacing a shifter, working on internal hub gears such as Shimano Nexus or Sturmey-Archer, or adjusting electronic groupsets. These need 
specific tools and experience, and mistakes can be expensive. Senior volunteers on duty are listed on the whiteboard by the entrance, and Márton is usually present on Wednesday and Saturday afternoons. Related pages: Cable Replacement, Chain Wear and Replacement, Indexing
 Internal Hubs.

Diagnosing Gear Shifting Problems

Wiki page for volunteer mechanics at the Pedálpont community bike workshop, Budapest District VIII. Owner: Márton Kerekes. Read this before working on a customer's derailleur, especially if you are in your first three months of volunteering.

Most bikes brought to Pedálpont with "gears not working" have a cable or adjustment problem, not a broken part. Our records for 2024 show that of 318 shifting complaints, only 41 needed a new derailleur or shifter. Volunteers who start replacing parts before diagnosing the cause waste the customer's money and our limited stock of second-hand components, so please follow the order of checks below.

Order of Checks

• Look at the derailleur hanger from behind the bike; a bent hanger makes everything else impossible to adjust.
• Shift through all gears on a stand and note exactly where the chain hesitates, skips or overshoots.
• Check the cable for fraying at the shifter and the clamp bolt, and for rust inside the housing.
• Test barrel adjuster tension in half-turn steps.
• Confirm the limit screws stop the chain from falling off at either end of the cassette.
• Inspect chain wear with the gauge; a stretched chain skips under load even if the shifting is perfect.

Common Causes and Fixes

If the chain hesitates when shifting to larger cogs, cable tension is usually too low; turn the barrel adjuster anticlockwise half a turn and retest. If it hesitates when shifting to smaller cogs, tension is too high. If shifting is sluggish in both directions and the lever feels stiff, the cable or housing is dirty or corroded and should be replaced, which costs the customer about 1,500 forints for a cable and housing from our stock.

A bent hanger is the most underestimated problem. Many bikes arrive after being laid on the ground on their right side, especially those parked at the Corvin-negyed racks. Use the hanger alignment tool on the blue wall board, and remember that aluminium hangers can crack if bent back too far. We keep replacement hangers for the most common frames in drawer 14.

When to Ask for Help

Ask a senior volunteer before replacing a shifter, working on internal hub gears such as Shimano Nexus or Sturmey-Archer, or adjusting electronic groupsets. These need specific tools and experience, and mistakes can be expensive. Senior volunteers on duty are listed on the whiteboard by the entrance, and Márton is usually present on Wednesday and Saturday afternoons.

Related pages: Cable Replacement, Chain Wear and Replacement, Indexing Internal Hubs.

Intel Array Building Blocks (also known as ArBB) was a C++ library developed by Intel Corporation for exploiting data parallel portions of programs to take advantage of multi-core processors, graphics processing units and Intel Many Integrated Core Architecture processors. ArBB provides a generalized vector parallel programming solution designed to avoid direct dependencies on particular low-level parallelism mechanisms or hardware architectures. ArBB is oriented to applications that require data-intensive mathematical computations. By default, ArBB programs cannot create data races or deadlocks. History Intel Ct was a parallel programming model developed by Intel in 2007 for its future multi-core processors as part of the Tera-Scale research program. In April 2009, Intel announced that "Ct [is] to appear in programmer tools by end of the year". On August 19, 2009, Intel acquired RapidMind, a privately held company founded and headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada. In September 2010, Intel Array Building Blocks (ArBB) were introduced as the result of the merger of Intel Ct and RapidMind technologies. The first version of ArBB supported Microsoft Windows and Linux, and Intel, Microsoft Visual C
++ and GCC C++ compilers.

In October 2012 the project was discontinued in favour of other Intel projects: Cilk Plus and Threading Building Blocks. See also Cilk/Cilk Plus

Hamarøy Church ( or ) is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Hamarøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Presteid. It is the church for the Hamarøy parish which is part of the Ofoten prosti (deanery) in the Diocese of Sør-Hålogaland. The white, modern, concrete church was built in a fan-shaped style in 1974 using plans drawn up by the architect Nils Toft. The church seats about 400 people.

History
Hamarøy Church is located on an old church site. The earliest existing historical records of the church date back to 1589, but the building wasn't new at that time. The old stave church was torn down in 1655 and replaced with a new building on the same site, about south of the present church site. It was a timber-framed cruciform design. In 1771, the church was inspected and described as "dilapidated", so planning began for a new replacement church. In 1775, the old church was torn down and a new cruciform church was constructed on the same site.

In 1814, this church served as an election church (). Together with more than 300 other parish churches across Norway, it was a polling station for elections to the 1814 Norwegian Constituent Assembly which wrote the Constitution of Norway. This was Norway's first national elections. Each church parish was a constituency that elected people called "electors" who later met together in each county to elect the representatives for the assembly that was to meet in Eidsvoll later that year.

In 1840, the church was renovated, including a new tower on the roof and a new sacristy. By royal decree on 28 October 1882, it was ordered to demolish Hamarøy's old church and build a new church with 700 seats on a site further to the north. So, in 1885, a new church was built about to the north of the old church. Another royal decree from 19 September 1885, ordered that after the new church was completed, the old church was taken down and moved to the village of Karlsøy on the nearby island of Finnøya where it was rebuilt and is now known as the Sagfjord Church. In October 1969, Hamarøy Church burned down after a lightning strike. The present church was completed in 1974 on the same site as the previous building.

Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( , ; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, engineer, inventor, businessman, and philanthropist. He is known for creating dynamite as well as having bequeathed his fortune to establish the Nobel Prize. He also made several important contributions to science, holding 355 patents in his lifetime. Nobel's most famous invention was dynamite, an explosive using nitroglycerin; it was patented in 1867. Nobel displayed an early aptitude for science and learning, particularly in chemistry and languages; he became fluent in six languages and filed his first patent at the age of 24. He embarked on many business ventures with his family, most notably owning the company Bofors, which was an iron and steel producer that he had developed into a major manufacturer of cannons and other armaments.

Nobel was later inspired to donate his fortune to the Nobel Prize institution, which would annually recognize those who "conferred the greatest benefit to humankind". The synthetic element nobelium was named a
fter him, and his name and legacy also survives in companies such as Dynamit Nobel and AkzoNobel, which descend from mergers with companies he founded. Nobel was elected a member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, which, pursuant to his will, would be responsible for choosing the Nobel laureates in physics and in chemistry.

Personal life Early life and education Alfred Nobel was born in Stockholm, United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway on 21 October 1833. He was the third son of Immanuel Nobel (1801–1872), an inventor and engineer, and Karolina Andriette Nobel (née Ahlsell 1805–1889). The couple married in 1827 and had eight children. The family was impoverished and only Alfred and his three brothers survived beyond childhood. Through his father, Alfred Nobel was a descendant of the Swedish scientist Olaus Rudbeck (1630–1702), and in his turn, the boy was interested in engineering, particularly explosives, learning the basic principles from his father at a young age. Alfred Nobel's interest i

n technology was inherited from his father, an alumnus of Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm.Following various business failures caused by the loss of some barges of building material, Immanuel Nobel was forced into bankruptcy, Nobel's father moved to Saint Petersburg, Russia, and grew successful there as a manufacturer of machine tools and explosives. He invented the veneer lathe (which made possible the production of modern plywood) and started work on the torpedo. In 1842, the family joined him in the city. Now prosperous, his parents were able to send Nobel to private tutors and the boy excelled in his studies, particularly in chemistry and languages, achieving fluency in English, French, German and Russian. For 18 months, from 1841 to 1842, Nobel went to the only school he ever attended as a child, in Stockholm. Nobel gained proficiency in Swedish, French, Russian, English, German, and Italian. He also developed sufficient literary skill to write poetry in English. His Nemesis is a prose tragedy in four acts about the Italian noblewoman Beatrice Cenci. It was printed while he was dying, but the entire stock was destroyed immediately after his death except for three copies, being regarded as scandalous and blasphemous. It was published in Sweden in 2003 and has been translated into Slovenian, French, Italian, and Spanish.

Religion Nobel was Lutheran and regularly attended the Church of Sweden Abroad during his Paris years, led by pastor Nathan Söderblom who received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1930. He was an agnostic in youth and became an atheist later in life, though he still donated generously to the Church.

John Bernard "Jack" O'Reilly Jr. (bor
n September 21, 1948) is an American retired politician who served as the 6th mayor of Dearborn, Michigan from 2007 to 2022. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served on the Dearborn City Council from 1990 to 2007. Career

Dearborn City Council

O'Reilly Jr. began his political career serving as a city councilmen for Dearborn for 17 years between 1990 and 2007. Mayor of Dearborn Following the passing of mayor Michael Guido from cancer O'Reilly was appointed the interim mayor until a special election could be held. He proceeded to run as a candidate during the special election and won and would be sworn in as a full mayor on February 27, 2007. As mayor he greatly improved the city's public infrastructure, including the construction of the John D. Dingell Train Station in an effort to turn the city into a regional transportation hub. As mayor he also greatly streamlined the bureaucratic process in the city, cutting out red tape. In January 2019, Dearborn Historian editor Bill McGraw had his contract terminated for an Autumn 2018 issue concerning Henry Ford. That issue, concurrent with the 100th anniversary of Ford's acquisition of the Dearborn Independent newspaper, detailed the anti-Semitic influence that Ford infamously exerted. The city government's suppression of the issue received widespread exposure, with some calling for Dearborn officials and others related to Ford's industry to recognize the impact of Ford's antisemitism. As a result of the national publicity, the Dearborn Historical Commission held an emergency meeting in which the commission created a resolution that called for the end of censorship of the issue. At a municipal deposition on February 13, 2019 mayor O'Reilly was unable to answer basic personal questions, forgetting how many children he had, their names and ages, as well as stating he took his Bar exam in 1890. However, despite this he continued to serve as mayor for an additional two years until in another deposition on June 26, 2021, where he was too mentally unfit to even appear, instead having to issue all his statements through curated press releases. He would announce on July 9, 2021 that has been suffering from an undisclosed illness preventing him from making public appearances and that he will not be seeking another term as mayor retiring after 32 years of public s
ervice. Personal life

His family background includes an elected official. His father, John B. O'Reilly Sr., was mayor from 1978 to 1985 and also Dearborn Police Chief. He is married and has three sons.

Qingji was a nobleman during the Spring and Autumn period. He is portrayed differently in various historical records.

Life
The Zuo zhuan records Qingji as a member of the clan of King Fuchai of Wu, often admonishing the king to change his ways of governing in order to avoid calamities for the state of Wu.

Zuo zhuan relates that after his advice was ignored, Qingji left the capital Gusu, moved to Aidi (in today's Jiangxi province), and finally took the chance to move into the state of Chu.

According to the Spring and Autumn Annals of Wu and Yue, Qingji was the son of King Liao of Wu, and a warrior of Wu.

Death
According to the Zuo zhuan, in the winter of 475 BC, Qingji heard that the state of Yue was about to attack his homeland of Wu. He went back to Wu in order to arrange peace talks with Yue. Upon his return, he tried to eliminate Wu's disloyal people and obtain Yue's favor, for which he was murdered by a man of Wu.

A more famous and detailed story of his death appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals of Wu and Yue's biography of King Helü of Wu. According to this story, King Helü was threatened at the beginning of his regime by Qingji's well-known bravery, and assigned a loyalist named Yao Li to murder him. Yao Li was given a public image of a person who endured great suffering under King Helü, substantiated by some pre-planned actual suffering such as imprisonment, the murder of his family, and cutting off his arm, so that he could obtain Qingji's trust. Qingji did in fact come to trust Yao Li, and during a joint boat trip, Yao Li murdered Qingli with a spear, and then committed suicide.

Monster by the same name
Curiously enough, in the book Guanzi the same name, Qingji, is used to denote a monster having a human form four fingers high, riding a small horse. This monster is the product of lakes being dry for a few hundreds of years.

Career

Albert studied at the university of Frankfurt (Oder), and in 1513 became Archbishop of Magdeburg at the age of 23 and administrator of the Diocese of Halberstadt.

In 1514 he was also elected Archbishop of Mainz and thus sovereign of the Electorate of Mainz and archchancellor of the Holy Roman Empire. By electing him, the Mainz cathedral chapter hoped for the support of the Elector of Brandenburg in defending the city of Erfurt, which belonged to the archbishopric of Mainz, against the expansionist efforts of the neighboring Saxon dukes. Albert also did not meet the requirements for taking over any diocese, since he had not yet reached the age, and he didn't have a college degree; therefore he received a study dispensation in 1513. Albert borrowed 20,000 guilders from Jacob Fugger to pay the confirmation fee to the Roman Curia (see: simony). Later, Martin Luther addressed a letter of protest to Albert concerning the conduct of Tetzel.

Luther sent these to Albert on 31 October 1517, and according to a disputable tradition, nailed a copy to the door of Castle Church in Wittenberg. Albert forwarded the theses to Rome, suspecting Luther of heresy.

As Archbishop of Mainz, he tried unsuccessfully in 1515 and 1516 to expel the Jews living in Mainz. In 1518, at the age of 28, he was made a cardinal. When the imperial election of 1519 drew near, partisans of the two leading candidates (kings Charles I of Spain and Francis I of France) eagerly solicited the vote of the Prince-Archbishop of Mainz, and Albert appears to have received a large amount of money for his vote. The electors eventually chose Charles, who became the Emperor Charles V.

Like other high-ranking clergymen of his time, Archbishop Albert lived in concubinage, gave his lovers gifts and favored his children as far as possible without causing much offense. Recent research assumes that he lived in a marriage-like relationship at first with Elisabeth "Leys" Schütz from Mainz and then with the Frankfurt widow Agnes Pless, née Strauss. With Leys Schütz he had a daughter named Anna, whom he married to his secretary Joachim Kirchner.

The Anadyr (; Yukaghir: Онандырь; ) is a river in the far northeast of Siberia which flows into the Gulf of Anadyr of the Bering Sea and drains much of the interior of Chukotka Autonomous Okrug. Its basin corresponds to the Anadyrsky District of Chukotka. Geography The Anadyr is long and has a basin of . It is frozen from October to late May and has a maximum flow in June with the snowmelt. It is navigable in small boats for about to near Markovo. West of Markovo it is in the Anadyr Highlands (moderate mountains and valleys with a few trees) and east of Markovo it moves into the Anadyr Lowlands (very flat treeless tundra with lakes and bogs). The drop from Markovo to the sea is less than . It rises at about 67°N latitude and 171°E longitude in the Anadyr Highlands, near the headwaters of the Maly Anyuy, flows southwest receiving the waters of the rivers Yablon and Yeropol, turns east around the Shchuchy Range and passes Markvovo and the old site of Anadyrsk, turns north and east and receives the Mayn from the south, thereby encircling the Lebediny Zakaznik, turns northeast to receive the Belaya from the north in the Parapol-Belsky Lowlands, then past Ust-Belaya it turns southeast into the Anadyr Lowlands past the Ust-Tanyurer Zakaznik and receives the Tanyurer from the north. At Lake Krasnoye, it turns east and flows into the Onemen Bay of the Anadyr Estuary. If the Onemen Bay is considered part of the river, it also receives the Velikaya from the south and the Kanchalan from the north. Other important tributaries are the Yablon, Yeropol and Mamolina from the right and the Chineyveyem and Ubiyenka from the left. Its basin is surrounded by the Amguema and Palyavaam basins to the north, the Bolshoy Anyuy, Oloy and Kolyma basins to the northwest, and the Penzhina basin to the southwest.

History In 1648, Semyon Dezhnev reached the mouth of the Anadyr after being shipwrecked on the coast. In 1649, he went upriver and built winter quarters at Anadyrsk. For the next 100 years, the Anadyr was the main route from the Arctic to the Pacific and Kamchatka. In the 18th century, the Anadyr was described by the polar explorer Dmitry Laptev.

Ecology
The country through which it passes is thinly populated, and is dominated by tundra, with a rich variety of plant life. Much of the region's landscapes are dominated by rugged mountains. For nine months of the year the ground is covered with snow, and the frozen rivers become navigable roads. George Kennan, an American working on the Western Union Telegraph Expedition in the late 1860s, found that dog sled travel on the lower Anadyr was limited by lack of firewood. Reindeer, upon which the local inhabitants subsisted, were once found in considerable numbers, but the domestic reindeer population has collapsed dramatically since the reorganization and privatization of state-run collective farms beginning in 1992. As herds of domestic reindeer have declined, herds of wild caribou have increased. There are ten species of salmon inhabiting the Anadyr river basin. Ev
ery year, on the last Sunday in April, there is an ice fishing competition in the frozen estuarine waters of the Anadyr's mouth. This festival is locally known as Korfest. The area is a summering place for a number of migratory birds including brent geese, Eurasian wigeons, and the pintails of California.

See also Operation Anadyr

The Anadyr (; Yukaghir: Онандырь; ) is a river in the far northeast of Siberia which flows into the Gulf of Anadyr of the Bering Sea and drains much of the interior of Chukotka Autonomous Okrug. Its basin corresponds to the Anadyrsky District of Chukotka.

Geography
The Anadyr is long and has a basin of . It is frozen from October to late May and has a maximum flow in June with the snowmelt. It is navigable in small boats for about to near Markovo. West of Markovo it is in the Anadyr Highlands (moderate mountains and valleys with a few trees) and east of Markovo it moves into the Anadyr Lowlands (very flat treeless tundra with lakes and bogs). The drop from Markovo to the sea is less than .

It rises at about 67°N latitude and 171°E longitude in the Anadyr Highlands, near the headwaters of the Maly Anyuy, flows southwest receiving the waters of the rivers Yablon and Yeropol, turns east around the Shchuchy Range and passes Markvovo and the old site of Anadyrsk, turns north and east and receives the Mayn from the south, thereby encircling the Lebediny Zakaznik, turns northeast to receive the Belaya from the north in the Parapol-Belsky Lowlands, then past Ust-Belaya it turns southeast into the Anadyr Lowlands past the Ust-Tanyurer Zakaznik and receives the Tanyurer from the north. At Lake Krasnoye, it turns east and flows into the Onemen Bay of the Anadyr Estuary. If the Onemen Bay is considered part of the river, it also receives the Velikaya from the south and the Kanchalan from the north. Other important tributaries are the Yablon, Yeropol and Mamolina from the right and the Chineyveyem and Ubiyenka from the left.

Its basin is surrounded by the Amguema and Palyavaam basins to the north, the Bolshoy Anyuy, Oloy and Kolyma basins to the northwest, and the Penzhina basin to the southwest.

History
In 1648, Semyon Dezhnev reached the mouth of the Anadyr after being shipwrecked on the coast. In 1649, he went upriver and built winter quarters at Anadyrsk. For the next 100 years, the Anadyr was the main route from the Arctic to the Pacific and Kamchatka. In the 18th century, the Anadyr was described by the polar explorer Dmitry Laptev.

Ecology
The country through which it passes is thinly populated, and is dominated by tundra, with a rich variety of plant life. Much of the region's landscapes are dominated by rugged mountains. For nine months of the year the ground is covered with snow, and the frozen rivers become navigable roads. George Kennan, an American working on the Western Union Telegraph Expedition in the late 1860s, found that dog sled travel on the lower Anadyr was limited by lack of firewood.

Reindeer, upon which the local inhabitants subsisted, were once found in considerable numbers, but the domestic reindeer population has collapsed dramatically since the reorganization and privatization of state-run collective farms beginning in 1992. As herds of domestic reindeer have declined, herds of wild caribou have increased.

There are ten species of salmon inhabiting the Anadyr river basin. Every year, on the last Sunday in April, there is an ice fishing competition in the frozen estuarine waters of the Anadyr's mouth. This festival is locally known as Korfest.

The area is a summering place for a number of migratory birds including brent geese, Eurasian wigeons, and the pintails of California.

Operation Anadyr

Kōwhai Transit app, release runbook for version 5 onwards. Owner: Mobile Platform squad, Christchurch office. Questions go to Sione Feleti or Harriet Brandt. Why This Page Exists Our last three releases each hit a different snag, from a rejected App Store build to a crash in the Metro card top-up flow that reached 12 percent of Android users before anyone noticed. Most of those issues came from steps that someone knew about but had never
 written down. This runbook collects that knowledge so any engineer on the squad can drive a release without needing to ask the person who did the last one. Release Cadence

We ship a regular release every second Wednesday. The branch is cut on the Monday of release week, QA runs Monday and Tuesday, and store submiss
ions happen Wednesday morning before 10 am so that Apple review usually completes the same day. Hotfixes can go out at any time but must still pass the smoke test suite. Pre-Submission Checklist * Version and build numbers bumped in both the iOS and Android projects * Release notes written in plain English and checked by the comms team * Feature flags for unfinished work confirmed as off in the production config * Smoke tests green on a physical iPhone 13 and a Samsung Galaxy A54 * Crash-free sessions above 99.5 percent on the beta track for at least 24 hours Staged Rollout Android releases go out at 5 percent on day one, 25 percent on day two, and 100 percent on day four if crash metrics stay flat. iOS uses phased release, which spreads the update over seven days automatically. Do not tick the option to release to everyone immediately unless the release fixes a security issue or a payment bug that is actively costing users money. Monitoring After Release

Whoever drives the release keeps the Crashlytics dashboard open for the rest of the day and checks it again on Thursday morning. Watch the top-up flow and journey planner in particular, since they generate most of our revenue and complaints. If crash-free sessions drop below 99 percent, pause the Android rollout from the Play Console and post in the squad channel. Rolling Back We cannot truly roll back a mobile release once users have it installed. The practical response
is to halt the staged rollout, disable the faulty feature through its remote flag if one exists, and prepare a hotfix build. Keep that in mind when deciding whether new code should sit
 behind a flag.

HRM 305 Recruitment and Selection, Session 5 Notes Lecturer: Mrs Wangari Kuria, Kenyatta University School of Business. Topic:
 redesigning a hiring process from first principles. These notes accompany the slides from Wednesday's session, which used the example of a mid-sized Nairobi logistics company to show how a hiring process can be rebuilt when the old one stops working. Students who missed the session should read the case study handout on Rafiki Freight before the next tutorial. The Case in Brief Rafiki Freight had grown from 60 to 240 employees in four years. Hiring was handled by branch managers, who recruited mostly through personal networks and interviewed candidates informally. By 2025, the company faced high turnover among new drive
rs and warehouse supervisors, complaints from staff about favouritism, and a labour dispute in its Mombasa branch over a contested promotion. The new human resources director, Mr Tsegaye Abebe, was asked to design a better process within six months. Starting with the Job, Not the Candidate Mrs Kuria stressed that Mr Abebe began by rewriting job descriptions, not by changing interviews. Many existing descriptions were copied from templates and listed duties that had nothing to do with the real work. For example, the warehouse supervisor de
scription required a degree in business administration but said nothing about managing night shifts or handling stock discrepancies, which were the most difficult parts of the role. Elements of the
New Process The redesigned process at Rafiki Freight introduced several features that the class discussed in detail: * A job
analysis interview with current post holders before any vacancy is advertised
* Written selection criteria, each linked to a specific part of the job * A work sample test, such as a mock stock count for warehouse supervisors or a supervised driving assessment for drivers * Structured interviews with the same questions asked of every candidate * Panellists recording their marks separately before comparing notes * A short probation review at three months, feeding back into the sele
ction criteria Evidence for Structured Methods Mrs Kuria summarised research showing that work samples and structured interviews predict job performance considerably better than unstructured interviews, which 

are often influenced by first impressions and similarity between interviewer and candidate. She warned students, however, that structured methods only work if managers follow them; at Rafiki, two branch managers continued to m
ake informal offers until the managing director required all offers 
to be signed by human resources. Results After the first year, early turnover among new drivers fell from 34 to 19 percent, and the staff survey showed a clear improvement in perceived fairness. Hiring took longer, averaging six weeks instead of two, which some managers resented.
Discussion Questions for Tutorial Consider whether the longer hiring time was a fair price for better outcomes, and how Mr Abebe might have reduced it. Also think about how the process should be adapted for casual workers hired during the peak season, when speed matters most.

HRM 305 Recruitment and Selection, Session 5 Notes

Lecturer: Mrs Wangari Kuria, Kenyatta University School of Business. Topic: redesigning a hiring process from first principles.

These notes accompany the slides from Wednesday's session, which used the example of a mid-sized Nairobi logistics company to show how a hiring process can be rebuilt when the old one stops working. Students who missed the session should read the case study handout on Rafiki Freight before the next tutorial.

The Case in Brief

Rafiki Freight had grown from 60 to 240 employees in four years. Hiring was handled by branch managers, who recruited mostly through personal networks and interviewed candidates informally. By 2025, the company faced high turnover among new drivers and warehouse supervisors, complaints from staff about favouritism, and a labour dispute in its Mombasa branch over a contested promotion. The new human resources director, Mr Tsegaye Abebe, was asked to design a better process within six months.

Starting with the Job, Not the Candidate

Mrs Kuria stressed that Mr Abebe began by rewriting job descriptions, not by changing interviews. Many existing descriptions were copied from templates and listed duties that had nothing to do with the real work. For example, the warehouse supervisor description required a degree in business administration but said nothing about managing night shifts or handling stock discrepancies, which were the most difficult parts of the role.

Elements of the New Process

The redesigned process at Rafiki Freight introduced several features that the class discussed in detail:

* A job analysis interview with current post holders before any vacancy is advertised
* Written selection criteria, each linked to a specific part of the job
* A work sample test, such as a mock stock count for warehouse supervisors or a supervised driving assessment for drivers
* Structured interviews with the same questions asked of every candidate
* Panellists recording their marks separately before comparing notes
* A short probation review at three months, feeding back into the selection criteria

Evidence for Structured Methods

Mrs Kuria summarised research showing that work samples and structured interviews predict job performance considerably better than unstructured interviews, which are often influenced by first impressions and similarity between interviewer and candidate. She warned students, however, that structured methods only work if managers follow them; at Rafiki, two branch managers continued to make informal offers until the managing director required all offers to be signed by human resources.

Results

After the first year, early turnover among new drivers fell from 34 to 19 percent, and the staff survey showed a clear improvement in perceived fairness. Hiring took longer, averaging six weeks instead of two, which some managers resented.

Discussion Questions for Tutorial

Consider whether the longer hiring time was a fair price for better outcomes, and how Mr Abebe might have reduced it. Also think about how the process should be adapted for casual workers hired during the peak season, when speed matters most.

Subject: How we'll hire from November onwards

Hi team leads,

Quick heads-up before Thursday's all-hands, where Carolina will present this formally. After the review we ran over the summer, we're changing how candidates move through our hiring process at the Recife and Porto offices. I'd rather you hear the details from me now than be surprised in front of your teams.

Why We're Changing

Our average time from application to offer this year was 47 days. In exit surveys from candidates who withdrew, the most common reason was that another company made an offer while they were still waiting for our second interview. We also found that interview feedback arrived in eleven different formats, which made it very hard for the hiring committee to compare people fairly.

The New Stages

From 3 November, every engineering and product role will follow the same sequence:

- A 20-minute screening call with someone from talent acquisition
- A paid take-home exercise of no more than three hours, compensated at R$ 300
- A single interview loop of up to three conversations held on the same day
- A hiring committee decision within two working days of the loop

The take-home exercise replaces the live coding round. Several of you argued that live coding mostly measured how well people perform under observation, and the pilot run by Vítor's team in Porto supports that: candidates hired through the take-home route scored higher at their six-month review than those hired through live coding last year.

What This Means for You

Interviewers will now use one scorecard in Greenhouse with five criteria and a short written justification for each score. Please make sure everyone on your team who interviews completes the 45-minute calibration session that Débora Fontes is running on 22 and 29 October. Nobody can sit on a loop after 3 November without it.

We're also asking each team to nominate two people who can be available for same-day loops at least twice a month. I know that's a real commitment, but bunching conversations into one day is the single biggest change in reducing the wait for candidates.

Open Questions

We haven't finalised how internal transfers fit into this. For now, internal candidates skip the screening call but follow the rest of the process. If you have strong views on that, bring them on Thursday or message me directly.

Thanks for the feedback many of you gave during the review. Quite a lot of what's above came straight from your comments.

Talk soon,
Marta Sequeira, head of people operations

Shiori OPAC Release Notes Shiori is the public catalogue interface used by the Fukushima Prefectural Library and nineteen municipal libraries in the prefecture's shared network. The n
otes below describe recent releases and explain the reasoning behind each change, so that branch staff can answer questions from patrons and so that member libraries can decide when to update their local settings

. Release 7.3 (29 September 2026) • Search results now group different editions of the same work under a single entry • Holdings display shows the number of reservations waiting for each title • Furigana readings are matched when patrons search using hiragana only • The advanced search form adds a filter for large-print and audio formats Grouping editions was the most requested change in the 2025 patron survey. Previously, a search for a popular novel could return a dozen separate entries for hardback, paperback, pocket edition and large print, pushing other relevant titles down the page. The new grouping uses work identifiers supplied by the National Diet Library where available, and falls back to matching title and author readings. Catalogue manager Tomoko Shiga warns that grouping is less reliable for older books without work identifiers, and staff
 should report incorrect groupings through
 the usual err
or form. Showing reservation queues was a decision discussed at length by the network's steering group. Some members worried that long queues would discourage patrons, while others argued that patrons would rather know in advance. A three-month trial at Koriyama and Iwaki libraries found that reservations for titles with long queues actually increased slightly, and the change was rolled out network-wide. Release 7.2 (10 June 2026) • Added a contrast mode and adjustable text size for patrons with low vision • Fixed an error where items in transit between libraries showed as missing
• Improved loading speed of the home page on mobile networks

The accessibility changes were developed with the Fukushima Association of the Visually Impaired, whose members tested several designs at the prefectural library in May. The transit fix addresses a problem that had generated a steady stream of anxious calls from patrons who saw their reserved book marked as missing while it was actually on a delivery van 
between Aizuwakamatsu and the central sorting room. Release 7.1 (18 February 2026) • Introduced single sign-on with the prefecture's resident portal • Removed support for browsers more than three years old • Added a printable reading history for patrons who request it Single sign-on lets residents use one account for library services and other prefectural services, but local library cards still work as before. Shiori OPAC Release Notes

Shiori is the public catalogue interface used by the Fukushima Prefectural Library and nineteen municipal libraries in the prefecture's shared network. The notes below describe recent releases and explain the reasoning behind each change, so that branch staff can answer questions from patrons and so that member libraries can decide when to update their local settings.

Release 7.3 (29 September 2026)

• Search results now group different editions of the same work under a single entry
• Holdings display shows the number of reservations waiting for each title
• Furigana readings are matched when patrons search using hiragana only
• The advanced search form adds a filter for large-print and audio formats

Grouping editions was the most requested change in the 2025 patron survey. Previously, a search for a popular novel could return a dozen separate entries for hardback, paperback, pocket edition and large print, pushing other relevant titles down the page. The new grouping uses work identifiers supplied by the National Diet Library where available, and falls back to matching title and author readings. Catalogue manager Tomoko Shiga warns that grouping is less reliable for older books without work identifiers, and staff should report incorrect groupings through the usual error form.

Showing reservation queues was a decision discussed at length by the network's steering group. Some members worried that long queues would discourage patrons, while others argued that patrons would rather know in advance. A three-month trial at Koriyama and Iwaki libraries found that reservations for titles with long queues actually increased slightly, and the change was rolled out network-wide.

Release 7.2 (10 June 2026)

• Added a contrast mode and adjustable text size for patrons with low vision
• Fixed an error where items in transit between libraries showed as missing
• Improved loading speed of the home page on mobile networks

The accessibility changes were developed with the Fukushima Association of the Visually Impaired, whose members tested several designs at the prefectural library in May. The transit fix addresses a problem that had generated a steady stream of anxious calls from patrons who saw their reserved book marked as missing while it was actually on a delivery van between Aizuwakamatsu and the central sorting room.

Release 7.1 (18 February 2026)

• Introduced single sign-on with the prefecture's resident portal
• Removed support for browsers more than three years old
• Added a printable reading history for patrons who request it

Single sign-on lets residents use one account for library services and other prefectural services, but local library cards still work as before. Support questions should be directed to the network help desk in Fukushima city, open on weekdays from 9:00 to 17:00.

How to Watch a Rocket Launch From Naro Space Center Safely and Legally Watching a launch from Goheung is one of the most memorable things you can do in South Jeolla province, but it takes planning. Launch dates move, roads close,
 and the best viewing spots fill up hours early. This tutorial explains how to prepare, where to watch and what to expect, based on my experience at four launches since 2022. I am Bui Quang Hieu, a
Vietnamese engineering student at Chonnam National University, and I first went with my lab mates Kim Ga-eun and Shin Tae-oh to watch the Nuri rocket. Step 1: Track the Launch Date The Korea Aerospace Research Institute announces launch windows about a month ahead, but the exact day is confirmed only a day or two before launch, depending on weather and technical checks. Follow the institute's official social media accounts and the Goheung county website,
which posts road closure notices. Book accommodation that allows free cancell
ation, because a delay of two or three days is common. Step 2: Choose a Viewing Spot The launch centre itself is closed to the public on launch
day, and a safety zone extends several kilometres around it. Public viewing is possible from designated sites that the county prepares. Popular options include: • Namyeolhae beach, about 17 kilometres from the launch pad, with a clear view across the water and a large parking area. • The Goheung Space Science Center observation deck, which has screens showing the countdown but fills up very early. • Uju Observatory park on the hill above Namyeol, popular with photographers for its elevated view. • Fishing villages along the Bongnae peninsula coast, which are quieter but may be inside temporary access restrictions. Step 3: Plan Your Arrival Roads into the Bongnae area close several hours before launch, typically from mid-morning for an a
fternoon launch. Arrive before closu

res begin, or park at the official shuttle points in Goheung town. When we went in 2023, we arrived at Namyeolhae at 08:00 for a 18:24 launch and found the parking lot already half full. Step 4: Bring the Right Equipment You will wait outdoors for many hours, so bring water, food, sunscreen and a folding chair. Binoculars help you see the rocket before liftoff, though from 17 kilometres it is small until the engines ignite. If you want photographs, use a telephoto lens of at least 300 millimetres and a tripod. A battery pack for your phone is essentia
l, since you will probably watch the official livestream while waiting. Step 5: Enjoy and Stay Safe When the rocket lifts off, you will see the flame first and hear the roar about 50 seconds later because sound travels slowly over that distance. Stay at your viewing site until the official announcement that the launch phase is over, as authorities sometimes keep areas closed until debris falls into the sea zones. Leaving afterward can take two or three hours because of traffic, so be patient or stay for dinner in Goheung.

• Uju Observatory park on the hill above Namyeol, popular with photographers for its elevated view.
• Fishing villages along the Bongnae peninsula coast, which are quieter but may be inside temporary access restrictions.

Roads into the Bongnae area close several hours before launch, typically from mid-morning for an afternoon launch. Performance Review of Commercial Rooftop Solar Installations, Kalmar County, 2023-2026

Report KR-SOL-07 from the Energy Office of Kalmar County, prepared by Patrik Sundqvist and Emma Rydén. Published 29 September 2026. 1 Purpose of the Review

Between 2023 and 2025, 142 businesses in Kalmar County installed rooftop solar systems with support from the regional green investment programme. The programme required each recipient to share production data for three years. This report compares actual production with the forecasts made at the time of installation and examines which factors explain the differences, in order to improve guidance for future applicants. 2 Installations Studied The sample includes systems ranging from 15 to 480 kilowatts peak on warehouses, farm buildings, shops and small factories. Most are located on the mainland around Kalmar, Nybro and Oskarshamn, with eleven on Öland. Systems we
re installed by nine different contractors and use panels from six manufacturers. 3 Results

On average, systems produced 94 percent of their forecast annual output, with a wide spread from 71 to 112 percent. Systems on Öland performed best, benefiting from the island's 
high number of sunshine hours. Underperformance was concentrated among a minority of installations, and our analysis identified the most common causes as follows: 1. Shading from ventilation units, chimneys or neighbouring buildings that was not considered in the original design. 2. Inverter faults that went unnoticed for several weeks because nobody was monitoring the system.
3. Snow cover in winter on low-pitched roofs, which reduced production during January and February.
4. Soiling from dust and bird droppings on farm buildings close to grain handling areas. 5. Incorrect string configuration, leading to one string limiting the output of another.

4 The Monitoring Gap The most striking finding concerns monitoring. Among the 27 systems that produced less than 85 percent of their forecast, 19 had experienced an inverter fault lasting more than two weeks. In most of these cases, the business owner noticed the problem only when the electricity bill 
rose. Systems where the installer offered a monitoring service with automatic alerts had an average downtime of just three days per year. 5 Recommendations

We recommend that future programme rules require installers to provide at least five years of remote monitoring with automatic fault alerts. Applicants should receive a shading analysis based on a site visit, not only on aerial images, and installers should document string configurations in a standard format. For farm buildings, a cleaning plan should be agreed at installation. The Energy Office will update its guidance and hold an information meeting for installers in Kalmar on 4 November 2026.

Syllepte rogationis is a moth in the family Crambidae. It was described by George Hampson in 1918. It is found in Mozambique. The forewings are yellowish white, the costal area to the postmedial line, the inner margin (except towards base) and the terminal area red-brown. There is a diffused incurved red-brown subbasal line and the antemedial line is red-brown, oblique to the median nervure. There is a red-brown spot in the middle of the cell and a discoidal bar. The median nervure towards the extremity and a patch beyond the lower angle of the cell are red-brown, as is the postmedial line. This line is excurved between veins 5 and 2, then retracted to the lower angle of the cell and excurved to the inner margin. The inner edge of the red-brown terminal area is waved, excurved between veins 5 and 2, then expanding into a patch confluent with the postmedial line. The hindwings are yellowish white with an oblique brown discoidal bar. The veins beyond the lower angle of the cell are streaked with brown and the postmedial line is rather diffused red-b
rown, excurved between veins 5 and 2, then retracted to below the angle of the cell and ending above the inner margin. The terminal area is red-brown, its inner edge waved and excurved between veins 5 and 2.

Mission Report EOS-TK2: Launch and Early Orbit Phase of the Tana Earth Observation Satellite

Issued by the Flight Dynamics Group, Malindi Ground Segment, 3 March

1 Summary

The Tana-2 microsatellite lifted off at 04:12 UTC on 18 February aboard a rideshare mission from the equatorial pad, carrying a 42-kilogram multispectral imager built jointly by the Nairobi Space Systems Laboratory and partners at Bahir Dar Institute of Technology. Separation from the launch adapter occurred 61 minutes after liftoff, and the first telemetry pass over Malindi confirmed that the spacecraft was alive, power positive and tumbling slowly at under three degrees per second.

2 Orbit Achieved

The injection was close to nominal. The target was a 525-kilometre circular orbit at 97.4 degrees inclination; the two-line elements published the next day placed the satellite at 519 by 531 kilometres with an inclination within 0.02 degrees of plan. This dispersion is well inside the margin of the onboard cold-gas thruster, and the group decided that no correction burn is needed during the first year of operations.

3 Early Orbit Timeline

Commissioning proceeded in stages over the first fortnight. The key milestones recorded by the operations team were:

• Detumbling completed by the magnetorquers within 9 hours of separation
• Deployment of both solar wings confirmed by current readings on pass four
• Star tracker lock achieved on day two after a software parameter update
• First S-band downlink at the full 2 megabit per second rate on day five
• First-light images of Lake Turkana and the Omo delta received on day eleven

4 Anomalies

Two anomalies were logged. The first was a reset of the onboard computer during the third eclipse, traced to a watchdog timer set too short for the battery heater routine. Engineers uploaded a revised value on 21 February and no further resets have occurred. The second concerned an intermittent loss of the GPS receiver fix over the South Atlantic, which is consistent with known radiation effects in that region and is not considered a design defect.

Thermal readings have stayed within predicted ranges, with the imager focal plane holding between 12 and 17 degrees Celsius across sunlight and eclipse. Battery depth of discharge is averaging 18 percent per orbit, comfortably below the 30 percent limit set for a five-year mission life.

5 Next Steps

Calibration of the imager against ground targets in the Amboseli basin and at the Afar salt flats will run until the end of March, with field teams from both universities measuring surface reflectance during overpasses. Routine data distribution to the agricultural ministries in Kenya and Ethiopia is expected to begin on 1 April, subject to the outcome of the calibration review chaired by Dr Tigist Alemu.

The first commencement at Columbia University was held on June 21, 1758, when the university, then known as King's College, conferred seven degrees upon its first graduating class. Today, the university graduates several thousand students each year from its several undergraduate colleges, graduate schools, and affiliated institutions. University Commencement traditionally takes place on the third Wednesday of May. Commencement at Columbia takes place over several days as each school and affiliated institution of the university holds its own Class Day, and culminates in the University Commencement, when degrees are conferred en masse by the university president. The tradition of celebrating commencement over several days has been a point of consternation to parents and other attendees: John McCain, whose daughter Meghan M
cCain graduated from the university in 2007, upon being informed that commencement was a multi-day affair, reportedly asked, "How many fucking times do I have to go to fucking New York this week? How many fucking times can you fucking graduate from fucking Columbia?” Over several centuries, Columbia has developed a number of traditions around its commencement ceremonies. As a highly important
symbolic event, a number of individual commencements have become historically significant, either due to notable guests in attendance or occasionally violent disruptions, such as in 1811, when several students were arrested and the ceremonies were never completed due to rioting. Recent changes, such as the introduction of Multicultural Graduation Celebrations, have garnered sig
nificant political controversy.

History Overview
According t

o the New-
York Gazette, the university's 1758 commencement was "conducted with much eleg

ance and propriety." It began with an academic procession from the vestry room of the Trinity Church schoolhouse to St. George's Chapel, described as follows: "The President with his Honour the Lieutenant Governor, who graced the solemnity by his presence, were preceded by the candidates for Batchelors [sic] and Masters Degrees, with their heads uncovered, and were followed by the Governors of the College, the Clergy of all denominations in this City, and other gentlemen of distinction of this and the neighboring Provinces." This was followed by a salutatory address delivered by Samuel Provoost, two debates on metaphysics between graduating 
students, an oration in English, and a debate between honorary degree recipients on heliocentrism. The president of the college, Samuel Johnson, then conferred degrees upon the seven members of the class of 1758 and fourteen honorary degree recipients, bef
ore the ceremony was concluded by a valedictory oration. From 1785 to 1790, New York City served as the capital of the United States. Prior to 1797, the city also jointly served as the state capital with Kingston. During this period, the college's commencement
 ceremonies were often frequented by prominent politicians in the area. This includes the commencemen
t of 1786, which the entirety of the Continental Congress and both houses of the New York State Legisl
ature attended, and the commencement of 1789, which saw most of the new United States federal government attend, including George Washington, who had only been sworn in as president a week before, Vice-President John Adams, the Senate and House of Representatives, and members of the Supreme Court, in addition to
Governor George Clinton, and other high state officials.
